War of the Sicilian Vespers.aftermath: The war, fought between Christian powers over claims to European thrones, is seen by some sources as a sign of the end of the Crusading era, and an indicative sign of the degradation of papal powers over excommunication and indulgence.

War of the Sixth Coalition.aftermath: Napoleon was determined to fight on, proposing to march on Paris. His soldiers and regimental officers were eager to fight on. But Napoleon's marshals and senior officers mutinied. On 4 April, at Fontainebleau, Napoleon was confronted by his marshals and senior officers, led by Ney. They told the Emperor that they refused to march. Napoleon asserted that the army would follow him. Ney replied, "the army will obey its chiefs".
War of the Sixth Coalition.keyTerms: Battle of Leipzig (October 16-19, 1813); Treaty of Fontainebleau (April 11, 1814)

War of the Spanish Succession.outcome: Treaties of Utrecht, Rastatt, and Baden
War of the Spanish Succession.aftermath: upright=1.3|The Royal Navy destroys a Spanish fleet off Sicily, Cape Passaro, August 1718
War of the Spanish Succession.keyTerms: Treaty of Utrecht (April 11, 1713); Treaty of Rastatt (March 7, 1714)

War of the Third Coalition.aftermath:
upright=1.35|All the participants of the War of the Third Coalition. ]]
Austerlitz and the preceding campaign profoundly altered the nature of European politics. In three months, the French had occupied Vienna, decimated two armies, and humbled the Austrian Empire. These events sharply contrast with the rigid power structures of the 18th century, when no major European capital was ever held by an enemy army. Austerlitz set the stage for a near-decade of French domination on the European continent, but one of its more immediate impacts was to goad Prussia into war in 1806.
War of the Third Coalition.keyTerms: Battle of Austerlitz (December 2, 1805); Treaty of Pressburg (December 26, 1805)

Wars in Lombardy.outcome: Treaty of Lodi, compromise treaty leading to a balance of power and a period of stability
Wars in Lombardy.aftermath: Thirty years (1423-1454) of war among the great Italian powers — Milan, Venice, Florence, Naples, the Papacy — for dominance in northern Italy. The Peace of Lodi established the long Italian balance of power that lasted until the French invasions of the 1490s.

Wars of Alexander the Great.keyTerms: Battle of Gaugamela (October 1, 331 BC); Death of Alexander (June 10, 323 BC)
Wars of Alexander the Great.aftermath: Twelve years (336-323 BC) of conquest that destroyed the Achaemenid Persian Empire and extended Greek-Macedonian power from Egypt to the Punjab. Alexander's death without a clear heir produced the Diadochi wars and the Hellenistic kingdoms that shaped Eurasian politics for centuries.

Wars of the Diadochi.keyTerms: Battle of Ipsus (301 BC); Battle of Corupedium (281 BC)
Wars of the Diadochi.aftermath: Forty-six years (323-277 BC) of war among Alexander the Great's generals to partition his empire. The wars produced the Hellenistic kingdoms: the Antigonid (Macedon and Greece), Seleucid (Asia from the Aegean to the Indus), Ptolemaic (Egypt), and several smaller dynasties. These kingdoms shaped Mediterranean and Near Eastern politics until the Roman conquests.

Wars of the Three Kingdoms.aftermath: Having defeated all organised opposition, the Grandees of the Parliamentary New Model Army and their civilian supporters dominated the politics of all three nations for the next nine years (see Interregnum (1649–1660)). As for England, the Rump Parliament had already decreed it was a republic and a Commonwealth. Ireland and Scotland were now subjugated and ruled by military governors, and constituent representatives from both nations were seated in the Rump Parliament of the Protectorate, where they were dominated by Oliver Cromwell, the Lord Protector. When Cromwell died in 1658, control of the Commonwealth became unstable.
Wars of the Three Kingdoms.keyTerms: Execution of Charles I (January 30, 1649); Cromwellian Conquest (1649-1653)

Western Sahara War.aftermath: Sixteen years of war (1975-1991) between Morocco and the Polisario Front over the former Spanish Sahara. The UN-brokered ceasefire (1991) promised a referendum on self-determination that has never occurred. Morocco controls most of the territory behind a 2,700 km defensive berm.

Winter War.aftermath: Three months of war in which Finnish ski troops humiliated the Red Army before sheer numbers told. The poor Soviet performance encouraged Hitler's 1941 invasion plan. Finland's grievance over Karelia drove its entry into the Continuation War on the Axis side.

World War I.outcome: Armistice of Compiègne (11 November 1918, 11:00) ended fighting on the Western Front. The Allies (France, United Kingdom, United States, Italy, Russia until 1917) won.
World War I.aftermath: The Treaty of Versailles (1919) imposed reparations and territorial losses on Germany. The Austro-Hungarian, Ottoman, Russian, and German empires all collapsed and were replaced by republics or new states. ~20 million people died, roughly half of them civilians. The 1918 influenza pandemic, accelerated by wartime troop movement, killed another ~50 million. The League of Nations was founded but proved unable to prevent the next war.
World War I.keyTerms: Armistice (11 November 1918) followed by the Treaty of Versailles (28 June 1919), Treaty of Saint-Germain (Austria), Treaty of Trianon (Hungary), Treaty of Sèvres / Lausanne (Ottoman Empire).
notable: Collapse of four empires (German, Austro-Hungarian, Russian, Ottoman)
Creation of Poland, Czechoslovakia, Yugoslavia, and the Baltic states
Mandate system divides the former Ottoman lands
Russian Revolution removed Russia from the war in 1917

World War II.outcome: Unconditional surrender of Germany (8 May 1945) and Japan (2 September 1945). The Allies (Soviet Union, United States, United Kingdom, China, France) won.
World War II.aftermath: Germany was occupied and partitioned into four zones, which became West Germany and East Germany. Japan was occupied by the United States until 1952. ~70 to 85 million people died, roughly 3 percent of the 1940 world population. The Holocaust killed ~6 million Jews and ~5 million others. The United Nations replaced the League of Nations, the Bretton Woods system reshaped global finance, and the Soviet Union and United States emerged as the two postwar superpowers. The trial of Nazi leaders at Nuremberg established the precedent that aggressive war and crimes against humanity are individually prosecutable.
World War II.keyTerms: Unconditional surrender. Signed at Reims (7 May), ratified at Karlshorst (8 May) for Germany. Signed aboard USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay (2 September) for Japan.
notable: Nuremberg and Tokyo war crimes trials
Partition of Germany and creation of the United Nations
Start of the nuclear age following Hiroshima and Nagasaki
Beginning of the Cold War

World War II in Yugoslavia.aftermath: Four years (1941-1945) of multi-sided war among Axis occupiers, the Ustaše-led Independent State of Croatia, Mihailović's Chetniks, Tito's Partisans, and various nationalist forces. Approximately 1 million dead. The Partisan victory produced socialist Yugoslavia under Tito.

Yom Kippur War.aftermath: Analyses differ on the military outcome of the war. as an Israeli victory by some military historians,}} an Egyptian victory by other historians, and by others, as a military stalemate.
Yom Kippur War.outcome: Egyptian-Syrian initial gains reversed; Israel pushes within striking distance of Cairo and Damascus before UN ceasefire.

northern front of the Russian invasion o.aftermath: After Ukraine had fully retaken Kyiv Oblast, its military began to mop up pockets of isolated Russian troops who had been left behind in the retreat. The Institute for the Study of War assessed that these remnant groups did not offer organized resistance. The Institute for the Study of War also said that some of the Russian units that were pulled back to Belarus and western Russia would "remain combat ineffective for a protracted period".

Mongol invasions.outcome: Largest contiguous land empire in history; division into four khanates after Kublai's death.
Mongol invasions.aftermath: The Mongol conquests killed an estimated 40 million people across Eurasia, depopulated central Asia, and rewrote the political map from China to Hungary. The Pax Mongolica that followed reopened the Silk Road, carried Black Death westward, and put Europe in sustained contact with East Asia for the first time since antiquity.

Russia-Ukraine War.aftermath: A war that began in 2014 with the annexation of Crimea expanded in February 2022 into the largest European war since 1945. Russia controls the Donbas and southern strip; Ukraine retains its government, sovereignty, and a flow of Western weapons. NATO expanded to include Finland and Sweden in response.
Russia-Ukraine War.keyTerms: Russian recognition of Donetsk and Luhansk (February 21 2022); full-scale invasion (February 24 2022)

Seven Years' War.outcome: British and Prussian victory. Britain takes Canada, Bengal, and command of global trade.
Seven Years' War.aftermath: Often called the first world war for its global theatres — North America, the Caribbean, India, the Philippines, the West African coast. Britain became the dominant maritime empire; France lost most of its colonies; Prussia survived to become a great power. The war's debts in Britain produced the colonial taxation policies that triggered the American Revolution.

Boer War.outcome: British victory; Treaty of Vereeniging (1902) absorbs Boer republics into the British Empire.

Italian Campaign (World War II).outcome: Allied victory; German forces in Italy surrender April 29, 1945.
Italian Campaign (World War II).aftermath: Twenty months of slow, costly war up the Italian peninsula. Monte Cassino, Anzio, the Gothic Line. The campaign drained German divisions from the Eastern and Western fronts and ended with the execution of Mussolini and the surrender of Army Group C.

Western Front (World War II).outcome: Allied victory; Germany surrenders unconditionally May 7-8, 1945.
Western Front (World War II).aftermath: D-Day to VE Day in eleven months — the Normandy breakout, liberation of Paris, Market Garden, Bulge, Rhine crossings, fall of the Reich. 1.4 million dead across Allies, Germans, and civilians on the Western European battlefields.

Mediterranean and Middle East theatre of.outcome: Allied victory across the theatre; German and Italian forces driven from Africa by 1943, from Greece and Crete by 1944.
Mediterranean and Middle East theatre of.aftermath: Five years of war across North Africa, Greece, Crete, Italy, the Balkans, Syria, Iraq, Iran, and the Aegean. The campaigns secured Suez and the oil of the Middle East for the Allies, knocked Italy out of the war, and produced the post-war political maps of Greece, Yugoslavia, and the Levant.

Western Front (World War I).outcome: Allied victory after the Hundred Days Offensive; armistice November 11, 1918.
Western Front (World War I).aftermath: Four years of trench warfare on a 700-km line from the North Sea to Switzerland killed 5.5 million people. The Western Front's industrialized killing — gas, machine guns, barbed wire, artillery — became the template for "modern war" in the popular imagination.

Italian Front (World War I).outcome: Italian victory after Vittorio Veneto; Austria-Hungary signs armistice November 3, 1918.
Italian Front (World War I).aftermath: Three and a half years of mountain war between Italy and Austria-Hungary along the Isonzo and the Piave. 1.4 million dead. Italy's territorial gains under the Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye fell short of Allied promises, feeding the post-war nationalist disillusion that brought Mussolini to power.

Laotian Civil War.outcome: Pathet Lao victory; Lao People's Democratic Republic proclaimed December 2, 1975.
Laotian Civil War.aftermath: Fifteen years of war between the Pathet Lao (backed by Vietnam and the USSR) and the Royal Lao Government (backed by the US and Thailand). The Plain of Jars became the most heavily bombed place per capita in history. Communist takeover followed the fall of Saigon by months.

Cambodian Civil War.outcome: Khmer Rouge victory; Lon Nol government falls April 17, 1975.
Cambodian Civil War.aftermath: Five years of war that ended with the Khmer Rouge taking Phnom Penh days before the fall of Saigon. The genocide that followed (1.5–2 million Cambodian dead) is treated as a separate event from this war.

Sengoku period.outcome: Tokugawa victory; founding of the Edo shogunate after Sekigahara (1600) and the Siege of Osaka (1615).
Sengoku period.aftermath: A century and a half of warlord conflict ended with Tokugawa Ieyasu's consolidation, opening the 250-year peace of the Edo period. The period's castle towns, samurai code, and political institutions shaped modern Japanese identity to a degree few historical eras can match.
Sengoku period.keyTerms: Battle of Sekigahara (1600); Siege of Osaka (1615)

Mexican Revolution.outcome: PRI (then PNR) consolidates power after a decade of revolt. New constitution of 1917.
Mexican Revolution.aftermath: A decade of civil war and political violence ended Porfirio Díaz's thirty-year dictatorship and produced the constitution and one-party system that ruled Mexico into the 1990s. Two million dead; massive demographic disruption, agrarian land reform, and the emergence of the modern Mexican state.

First Italian War.outcome: French expulsion from Italy by 1498; status quo ante bellum.
First Italian War.aftermath: Charles VIII's invasion of Italy in 1494, the conquest of Naples, the formation of the League of Venice, and the French withdrawal. Five decades of Italian Wars followed.

Wars of the Roses.outcome: Tudor victory at Bosworth Field (August 1485); Henry VII founds the Tudor dynasty.
Wars of the Roses.aftermath: Three decades of dynastic war between the houses of Lancaster and York exhausted the English nobility and concentrated power in the Crown — the precondition for Tudor centralisation, the Henrician Reformation, and Elizabethan ascendancy.

Onin War.outcome: Stalemate; Ashikaga shogunate authority destroyed and the Sengoku period begins.
Onin War.aftermath: Ten years of war within Kyoto that destroyed the capital and broke the central authority of the Ashikaga shogunate. The war is conventionally dated as the beginning of the Sengoku Jidai — the warring states period that lasted until Tokugawa unification.

Sri Lankan Civil War.outcome: Government victory; LTTE defeated and Velupillai Prabhakaran killed (May 2009).
Sri Lankan Civil War.aftermath: Twenty-six years of war between the Sri Lankan government and the Tamil Tigers. 100,000 dead, mass civilian casualties in the war's 2008-2009 endgame, sustained allegations of war crimes still unresolved.

Boko Haram insurgency.outcome: Ongoing; Boko Haram split (2016) into Boko Haram and Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP).
Boko Haram insurgency.aftermath: A decade-and-a-half Salafi-jihadist insurgency in northeastern Nigeria, Lake Chad basin, and adjacent states. 50,000+ dead, two million displaced, the Chibok schoolgirls kidnapping (April 2014) that briefly made the war a global cause.

Yemeni Civil War.outcome: Ongoing as of late 2025; Houthi de-facto control of the north, internationally recognised government in the south.
Yemeni Civil War.aftermath: A decade of war that has produced what the UN has repeatedly called the world's worst humanitarian crisis. 380,000 dead, mostly from war-induced famine and disease, in a war complicated by Saudi-Emirati-Iranian proxy involvement.

Tigray War.outcome: Negotiated end; Pretoria Agreement (November 2022) restores federal authority over Tigray.
Tigray War.aftermath: Two years of war between the Ethiopian federal government (with Eritrean support) and the Tigray People's Liberation Front. 600,000 dead, massive humanitarian crisis, severe disruption of Ethiopian politics and the Horn of Africa balance.

Wars at the end of the Han dynasty.outcome: Han collapse and the rise of Cao Cao, Sun Quan, and Liu Bei as the three contending powers.
Wars at the end of the Han dynasty.aftermath: Decades of civil war and warlord conflict that began with the Yellow Turban Rebellion ended with the formal abdication of the last Han emperor in 220, opening the Three Kingdoms period. Massive population displacement; classical sources record losses on the order of 30 million.

An Lushan Rebellion.outcome: Tang victory after eight years. An Lushan dynasty collapses in succession warfare; Tang authority restored but permanently weakened.
An Lushan Rebellion.aftermath: One of the most catastrophic rebellions in world history by death count. Census records show population decline from 53 million to under 17 million between 754 and 764 — though much of that may reflect collapsed registration rather than literal deaths. The Tang dynasty survived but never recovered its grip on the provinces, ceding power to regional military governors (jiedushi) whose autonomy seeded the dynasty's ninth-century collapse.
An Lushan Rebellion.keyTerms: Execution of An Qingxu (759); death of Shi Chaoyi (763)

First French intervention in Mexico.outcome: French victory; Treaty of Veracruz (March 1839) settles claims.
First French intervention in Mexico.aftermath: The "Pastry War" — a French naval intervention to extract reparations from Mexico for property losses suffered by French citizens. Brief but humiliating for Mexico; the French navy blockaded Veracruz and bombarded San Juan de Ulúa.

Battle of the Atlantic.outcome: Allied victory; U-boat campaign defeated by mid-1943.
Battle of the Atlantic.aftermath: Six years of war in the Atlantic — the longest continuous campaign of WW2. ULTRA decrypts, escort carriers, long-range aircraft, and convoy doctrine eventually defeated the Wolfpacks. Without the Atlantic supply line, Britain could not have stayed in the war; without Allied shipping, D-Day was impossible.
Battle of the Atlantic.keyTerms: Black May (May 1943); decisive Allied technological lead

Eastern Front (Soviet Union).aftermath: See Eastern Front (World War II) — canonical entry.

Pacification of Manchukuo.outcome: Japanese consolidation; sporadic Chinese resistance suppressed by 1939.
Pacification of Manchukuo.aftermath: A decade of Japanese counter-insurgency in the puppet state of Manchukuo. Anti-Japanese guerrilla bands, including the People's Anti-Japanese Army that would produce Kim Il-sung, were eventually driven into the Soviet Union by Kwantung Army operations.

Three Kingdoms.outcome: Jin reunification of China under Sima Yan (Emperor Wu) in 280.
Three Kingdoms.aftermath: Sixty years of warlord war ended with brief reunification under the Jin, but the institutional damage produced four centuries of disunity (the Six Dynasties period). The era became the dominant subject of Chinese historical memory — the Romance of the Three Kingdoms (14th c.) shaped East Asian narrative culture into the present.

Great Northern War.outcome: Russian victory; Treaty of Nystad (1721) cedes Sweden's Baltic provinces to Russia.
Great Northern War.aftermath: Twenty-one years of war that ended Swedish great-power status and established Russia as the dominant Baltic power. Peter the Great's victory at Poltava (1709) was the turning point.
Great Northern War.keyTerms: Battle of Poltava (1709); Treaty of Nystad (1721)

Mexican-American War.outcome: US victory; Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo (February 2, 1848).

Viking invasions of England.outcome: Mixed; Anglo-Saxon kingdoms survive, but Danish rule under Cnut (1016-1042) and Norman conquest (1066) follow.
Viking invasions of England.aftermath: Three centuries of Viking raids, settlement, and conquest from 793 (Lindisfarne) to 1066 (Stamford Bridge) reshaped the political and linguistic landscape of England. The Danelaw, the unification of England under Wessex, the Anglo-Saxon institutional state — all responses to Viking pressure.

Third Silesian War (Seven Years' War).outcome: Prussian survival; Treaty of Hubertusburg (1763) restores status quo ante.

Wars of Scottish Independence.outcome: Scottish victory; Treaty of Edinburgh-Northampton (1328) recognises Scottish independence.
Wars of Scottish Independence.aftermath: Six decades of war between Scotland and England that produced Robert the Bruce's kingdom and the modern Scottish national identity. The Declaration of Arbroath (1320) is the foundational text of Scottish constitutional history.
Wars of Scottish Independence.keyTerms: Battle of Bannockburn (June 1314); Treaty of Edinburgh-Northampton (1328)

Nine Years' War.outcome: Inconclusive; Peace of Ryswick (1697) restores most pre-war borders.
Nine Years' War.aftermath: Nine years of war between Louis XIV's France and a Grand Alliance led by William III of England. The first true world war by some accounts — fought in Europe, North America (King William's War), the Caribbean, and India. Set the financial precedent for the Bank of England (1694) and the long 18th-century Anglo-French rivalry.

Campaign of France of the Sixth Coalitio.outcome: Coalition victory; Napoleon abdicates April 1814, exiled to Elba.
Campaign of France of the Sixth Coalitio.aftermath: Three months of brilliant but doomed defensive campaigning by Napoleon against four converging Allied armies. The fall of Paris on March 31 ended the war; the abdication at Fontainebleau began the Bourbon Restoration.

Croatian War of Independence.outcome: Croatian victory; Erdut Agreement (1995) and Dayton complete the war.
Croatian War of Independence.aftermath: Four years of war during which Croatia secured its independence from Yugoslavia and ultimately recaptured the Serb-held Krajina region in Operation Storm (August 1995). 22,000 dead, with sustained allegations of war crimes on both sides.

Anglo–Spanish War.outcome: Treaty of London (1604) ends formal hostilities.

Franco-Dutch War.outcome: French victory; Treaties of Nijmegen (1678-1679) cede Franche-Comté and Flemish towns to France.
Franco-Dutch War.aftermath: Six years of war that confirmed Louis XIV as Europe's dominant monarch and produced the borders of the modern Low Countries. The Dutch Republic survived but lost its informal hegemony; William III's defensive coalitions against France would dominate his life.

German campaign of the Sixth Coalition.outcome: Coalition victory at Leipzig (October 1813); French expelled from Germany.
German campaign of the Sixth Coalition.aftermath: The Battle of the Nations decided Napoleon's fate in central Europe. Saxon and Bavarian defections during the battle turned a French army of 200,000 into a routed remnant. Within months the Coalition was over the Rhine and into France.

Irish Rebellion.outcome: See Irish Confederate Wars / Cromwellian Conquest of Ireland.

Six-Day War.outcome: Israeli victory in six days; capture of the Sinai, Gaza, West Bank, East Jerusalem, and Golan Heights.
Six-Day War.aftermath: Tripled Israeli-controlled territory and produced the occupation that defines Israeli-Palestinian politics into the present. The war ended pan-Arab Nasserism as a regional ideology and pushed the Soviet Union into open arms-supply backing of the Arab states through the 1973 war.

Indo-Pakistani War of 1947.outcome: Ceasefire; UN-mediated Line of Control divides Kashmir.
Indo-Pakistani War of 1947.aftermath: The first war over Kashmir, begun by Pakistani-supported tribal lashkars and ended by UN mediation. The Line of Control still divides Kashmir between India and Pakistan and remains the world's most-militarised border.

Indo-Pakistani War of 1971.outcome: Indian-Bangladeshi victory; Pakistani Eastern Command surrenders December 16, 1971.

Bangladesh Liberation War.outcome: Bangladeshi victory with Indian military support; East Pakistan becomes independent Bangladesh on 16 December 1971.
Bangladesh Liberation War.aftermath: Nine months of war that began with the Pakistani military crackdown on Bengali nationalism in March 1971. India intervened in December after a Pakistani preemptive strike. Three million civilian dead by Bangladeshi estimates; massive refugee outflow into India; sustained India-Pakistan hostility.

Second Chechen War.outcome: Russian victory; Chechen separatist forces defeated by 2009.
Second Chechen War.aftermath: A decade of war and counter-insurgency in Chechnya that began with the Russian invasion of October 1999. The siege and destruction of Grozny, the Beslan school massacre (2004), and the assassination of Aslan Maskhadov shaped the Putin presidency and the Russian regional security state.

Yugoslav Wars.outcome: Federation dissolved; six successor states by 2008.
Yugoslav Wars.aftermath: A decade of war that broke socialist Yugoslavia into Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia, Macedonia, FR Yugoslavia (later Serbia + Montenegro), and Kosovo. 140,000 dead, the Srebrenica massacre, the NATO bombing of Serbia. The ICTY at The Hague produced the modern international criminal-justice apparatus.

Sino-Indian War.outcome: Chinese victory; status quo border claims; ongoing Aksai Chin and Arunachal Pradesh disputes.
Sino-Indian War.aftermath: A one-month war in October-November 1962 along the Sino-Indian Himalayan border. China declared a unilateral ceasefire after demonstrating overwhelming tactical superiority. The Line of Actual Control remains contested into the 2020s.

War of the Triple Alliance.outcome: Brazilian-Argentine-Uruguayan victory; Paraguay loses 60-70% of its population.
War of the Triple Alliance.aftermath: The bloodiest interstate war in Latin American history. Six years of war over Paraguay's claim to the Río de la Plata system killed perhaps 400,000 — most of Paraguay's adult male population. Paraguay's recovery took generations.

Gaza war.aftermath: The Hamas attack of October 7 2023 killed 1,200 Israelis and triggered the most destructive Israeli military operation since 1948, with Gaza casualty estimates exceeding 50,000. Regional escalation drew in Hezbollah, the Houthis, and Iran in direct strike exchanges through 2024.

Second Anglo-Boer War.outcome: British victory; Treaty of Vereeniging (1902) absorbs the Boer republics.
Second Anglo-Boer War.aftermath: See Second Boer War — canonical entry.

First Anglo-Boer War.outcome: Boer victory; Pretoria Convention (1881) restores South African Republic independence under British suzerainty.
First Anglo-Boer War.aftermath: A three-month war in 1880-1881 in which Boer commandos routed British regulars at Majuba Hill. The British defeat held Boer-British peace for two decades until the Second Anglo-Boer War.

Russo-Polish War (1654–1667).outcome: Russian gains; Truce of Andrusovo cedes left-bank Ukraine and Smolensk to Russia.
Russo-Polish War (1654–1667).aftermath: Thirteen years of war that broke the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth's eastern dominance. Cossack Ukraine became permanently divided along the Dnieper. Russian gains in Ukraine seeded the next two centuries of Russian-Polish struggle.

Anglo-Saxon settlement of Britain.outcome: Anglo-Saxon victory; seven kingdoms (the Heptarchy) emerge by the 8th century.
Anglo-Saxon settlement of Britain.aftermath: Three centuries of migration and conquest from the Roman withdrawal in 410 to the establishment of stable Anglo-Saxon kingdoms by 700. The Britons were pushed into Wales, Cornwall, and the north; Old English supplanted Brittonic across most of what is now England.
Anglo-Saxon settlement of Britain.keyTerms: Battle of Mons Badonicus (c. 500); end of Sub-Roman Britain

Scottish clan wars.outcome: Final clan-system suppression after the 1745 Jacobite rising.
Scottish clan wars.aftermath: Six centuries of intermittent clan war in the Scottish Highlands, ended by the post-Culloden Heritable Jurisdictions Act (1746) that abolished clan-chief judicial authority. Highland clearances in the following decades extinguished the clan system as a social structure.

Russo-Swedish War (1788–90).outcome: Inconclusive; Treaty of Värälä restores status quo ante bellum.

Mexican-Texas War.outcome: Texan victory; Republic of Texas independent 1836, annexed by the US 1845.

Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire.outcome: Spanish victory under Pizarro; last Inca pretender Tupac Amaru executed 1572.
Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire.aftermath: Forty years of conquest and pacification, beginning with Atahualpa's capture in 1532, ended the Inca state and integrated the Andes into the Spanish empire. Smallpox and the encomienda system devastated the indigenous population; 1.5 million dead by reasonable estimate. Silver from Potosí financed Habsburg Spain.
Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire.keyTerms: Execution of Atahualpa (1533); execution of Tupac Amaru (1572)

Spanish conquest of Yucatán.outcome: Spanish victory; last independent Maya city Nojpetén falls 1697.
Spanish conquest of Yucatán.aftermath: A 170-year conquest of the Maya lowlands, far longer and bloodier than the conquest of central Mexico. Disease and reduction-to-mission communities killed perhaps 500,000 Maya. The Caste War of Yucatán (1847-1901) was the final Maya rising against Spanish-criollo rule.

Crusader invasions of Egypt.aftermath: Three Crusader campaigns into Egypt in the 1160s, all defeated. The campaigns brought Saladin from Kurdish lieutenant to ruler of Egypt and Syria — the man who would retake Jerusalem at Hattin (1187).
Crusader invasions of Egypt.keyTerms: Saladin's rise as vizier of Egypt (1169)

Anglo-Spanish War (1585–1604).outcome: Inconclusive; Treaty of London ends formal hostilities.

First Anglo-Afghan War.outcome: British defeat; the Army of the Indus annihilated on the retreat from Kabul (January 1842).
First Anglo-Afghan War.aftermath: Four years of catastrophe in which the East India Company installed a puppet ruler in Kabul, then lost almost the entire army on the retreat — perhaps the worst British military disaster of the 19th century. The "Great Game" against Russia began in earnest.

Mukden Incident.outcome: Japanese victory; puppet state of Manchukuo established March 1932.
Mukden Incident.aftermath: The September 18, 1931 false-flag explosion on the South Manchurian Railway gave the Kwantung Army its pretext for the conquest of Manchuria. The League of Nations' Lytton Report condemned the seizure; Japan left the League and the lights began to go out across the Far East.

Pacific theatre of World War II.outcome: US-led Allied victory; Japan surrenders September 2, 1945.
Pacific theatre of World War II.aftermath: See Pacific Theatre of World War II — canonical entry.

Pacific Theatre of World War II.outcome: US-led Allied victory; Japan surrenders aboard USS Missouri (September 2, 1945).
Pacific Theatre of World War II.aftermath: Four years of carrier and island-hopping warfare ended with two atomic bombings and Japan's unconditional surrender. 30 million dead across the theatre, including the Sino-Japanese front. The US occupation of Japan (1945-1952) produced the post-war constitution and Japan's alignment in the Cold War.
Pacific Theatre of World War II.keyTerms: Instrument of Surrender aboard USS Missouri (September 2, 1945)

European theatre of World War II.outcome: Allied victory; unconditional German surrender at Reims and Karlshorst, May 1945.
European theatre of World War II.aftermath: Six years of war that ended with Soviet occupation of Eastern Europe, Allied division of Germany, and the geographic settlement that fixed the Cold War. 40 million dead across the European theatre, including the Holocaust.

Donghak Peasant Revolution and the First.outcome: Japanese victory; Shimonoseki and the modern Korea-Japan-China triangle established.
Donghak Peasant Revolution and the First.aftermath: See First Sino-Japanese War — canonical entry.

Iran-Contra Affair.outcome: Political scandal; not a war but a covert programme exposed in 1986.
Iran-Contra Affair.aftermath: A US covert arms-for-hostages programme that funded the Nicaraguan Contras through Iranian arms-sales proceeds, in violation of the Boland Amendment. The scandal nearly ended the Reagan administration; fourteen administration officials were indicted.

Wars of the Roman Republic.outcome: Roman dominance from Britain to the Tigris; transition to imperial monarchy under Augustus.
Wars of the Roman Republic.aftermath: Five centuries of conquest produced the Mediterranean-spanning empire and the constitutional collapse of the Republic. The Principate that followed inherited the institutions but moved power from the Senate to the Emperor. Cumulative death toll over the period exceeds five million.

Caesar's Civil War.outcome: Caesarian victory; Pompey killed in Egypt, Caesar dictator perpetuo before his March 44 BC assassination.
Caesar's Civil War.aftermath: Five years of civil war ended the Roman Republic in everything but name. Caesar's assassination by senators on the Ides of March produced the second round of civil war (43-31 BC) that ended with Augustus and the Principate.

Roman conquest of Britain.outcome: Roman victory by 96 AD; province of Britannia established to Hadrian's Wall.
Roman conquest of Britain.aftermath: Sixty years of conquest, revolts (Boudica 60-61 AD), and pacification produced the southern province that lasted until Roman withdrawal in 410 AD. The Roman road system, the urban grid, Latin Christianity all reached Britain through Britannia.

Pyrrhic War.outcome: Roman victory; Pyrrhus withdrew from Italy in 275 BC.
Pyrrhic War.aftermath: Six years of war in which Pyrrhus of Epirus came to the aid of Tarentum against Rome. His battlefield victories at Heraclea and Asculum were so costly that "Pyrrhic victory" became a phrase; his withdrawal left Rome master of southern Italy and primed for the First Punic War.

Egyptian–Canaanite wars.outcome: Egyptian dominance through the New Kingdom; Sea Peoples pressure ends Egyptian control 12th century BC.
Egyptian–Canaanite wars.aftermath: Four centuries of New Kingdom Egyptian campaigning in the Levant from Thutmose III through Ramesses III. The Bronze Age Collapse and the rise of the Sea Peoples ended Egyptian imperial presence in Canaan.
Egyptian–Canaanite wars.keyTerms: Battle of Megiddo (1457 BC); Battle of the Delta (c. 1175 BC)

Persian-Roman wars.outcome: Centuries of stalemate ended by Arab conquest of both sides 630s-650s.
Persian-Roman wars.aftermath: Seven centuries of intermittent war between Rome (then Byzantium) and Parthia (then Sasanian Persia). The wars exhausted both empires by the 7th century, leaving them ripe for the Arab conquests that ended Sasanian Persia outright and stripped Byzantium of Egypt, the Levant, and Anatolia's heartland.

Roman–Sasanian War.outcome: Byzantine victory under Heraclius (628); peace treaty negotiated with Kavadh II.
Roman–Sasanian War.aftermath: Twenty-six years of war (602-628) that both sides survived but neither could recover from. Within a decade of the peace the Arab armies were across both their frontiers — taking Damascus 635, Ctesiphon 637, Egypt 639-642.

Norman conquest of England.outcome: Norman victory at Hastings (October 1066); subjugation complete by 1071.
Norman conquest of England.aftermath: Five years of conquest that produced the Norman ruling class, the imposition of feudal land tenure across England, and the cultural Latinisation that built modern English from Old English-Norman French interaction. The Domesday Book (1086) catalogued the post-conquest settlement.

Hundred Years' War prequel.outcome: Tensions over Gascony, the Flemish wool trade, and Capetian intervention in Brittany set the stage for the formal outbreak in 1337.
Hundred Years' War prequel.aftermath: See Hundred Years' War — canonical entry.
Hundred Years' War prequel.keyTerms: Edward III's claim to the French throne (October 1337)

Ottoman wars in Europe.outcome: Ottoman expansion peaks under Suleiman (1566); retreat begins after Vienna (1683); Empire formally dissolved 1922.
Ottoman wars in Europe.aftermath: Six centuries of intermittent war from the Balkans to the gates of Vienna shaped Christian–Muslim political identity in Europe. The Ottoman millet system organised Balkan religious communities; its dissolution after WWI produced the ethnic-nationalist politics that exploded again in 1991.
Ottoman wars in Europe.keyTerms: Treaty of Sèvres (1920); Treaty of Lausanne (1923)

Spanish conquest of Peru.outcome: Spanish victory; last Inca pretender Tupac Amaru executed 1572.
Spanish conquest of Peru.aftermath: Same arc as Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire — Atahualpa captured 1532, decades of pacification, Potosí silver financing Habsburg Spain.

Russo-Crimean Wars.outcome: Russian victory by 1783; Crimean Khanate annexed to Russia.
Russo-Crimean Wars.aftermath: Two and a half centuries of war and slave-raiding by the Crimean Tatars ended with Catherine II's 1783 annexation of the Khanate. Estimated three million slaves taken to Crimea over the centuries; their descendants form the Crimean Tatar diaspora.

Italian unification.outcome: Italy unified between 1859 and 1871; Rome the last capital absorbed.

Wars of Italian Independence.outcome: Italian victory across the three wars; Italian unification completed 1861-1871.
Wars of Italian Independence.aftermath: See Wars of Italian Unification — same arc.

Wars of German Unification.outcome: Prussian victory in three wars (Schleswig 1864, Austria 1866, France 1870-71); German Empire proclaimed 1871.
Wars of German Unification.aftermath: Three wars in seven years that produced the German Empire and the European balance-of-power system that would last until 1914. The exclusion of Austria from German leadership and the annexation of Alsace-Lorraine shaped the diplomatic landscape into World War I.
Wars of German Unification.keyTerms: Proclamation of the German Empire at Versailles (January 18, 1871)

Third Carlist War.outcome: Royal (Bourbon) victory; Carlists defeated and Carlos VII flees to France (1876).
Third Carlist War.aftermath: Four years of Carlist civil war that ended pretender claims in Spain. The Constitution of 1876 restored the Bourbons under Alfonso XII and inaugurated the long-running Restoration regime.

Banana Wars.outcome: US dominance of Caribbean basin states by 1934.
Banana Wars.aftermath: Three decades of US military interventions in Cuba, Haiti, Dominican Republic, Nicaragua, Honduras, and Mexico. The Marine Corps Small Wars Manual (1940) was the doctrinal legacy. FDR's Good Neighbor Policy ended the era in 1934.

Rif War.outcome: Spanish-French victory; Abd al-Krim surrenders May 1926.
Rif War.aftermath: A six-year colonial war in the Rif mountains of Morocco. Abd al-Krim's defeat of the Spanish at Annual in 1921 (10,000 Spanish dead) was one of the worst defeats of a colonial power in the era. The combined Franco-Spanish offensive used mustard gas extensively — the first chemical attack on civilians in colonial war.

Turkish War of Independence.outcome: Turkish victory under Atatürk; Treaty of Lausanne replaces Sèvres.
Turkish War of Independence.aftermath: A three-year war that destroyed the Greek expedition into Anatolia, replaced the Ottoman sultanate with the Turkish Republic, and produced the population exchange that ended Greek presence in Asia Minor after three millennia. Turkey's borders since are essentially those Lausanne fixed.

Russian invasion of Finland (1939–1940).outcome: Soviet victory; Moscow Peace Treaty cedes Karelia, Finland retains independence.

Suez Crisis.outcome: Israeli-British-French military victory but diplomatic defeat; UN-supervised withdrawal.
Suez Crisis.aftermath: A ten-day war following Nasser's nationalisation of the Suez Canal. US and Soviet pressure forced the withdrawal of the invading forces. The crisis marked the end of British and French status as great powers and confirmed US-Soviet primacy in the Middle East.

Bay of Pigs Invasion.outcome: Cuban victory; exile brigade defeated within 72 hours.
Bay of Pigs Invasion.aftermath: A CIA-organised invasion by 1,500 Cuban exiles, defeated by Castro's forces within three days. The disaster damaged the Kennedy administration's credibility and pushed Castro into a closer alliance with the Soviet Union — setting the stage for the Cuban Missile Crisis eighteen months later.

Dominican Civil War.outcome: US intervention restores order; constitutional government under Joaquín Balaguer 1966.
Dominican Civil War.aftermath: A six-month civil war in 1965 between constitutionalist supporters of ousted president Juan Bosch and the military junta. President Johnson sent 23,000 troops in Operation Power Pack — the largest US Caribbean intervention since the Banana Wars era.

Football War.outcome: Salvadoran tactical victory; OAS-brokered ceasefire restored pre-war borders.
Football War.aftermath: A four-day war between El Salvador and Honduras in July 1969, triggered by the deportation of Salvadoran settlers from Honduras and exacerbated by football qualifiers. The war's real causes were demographic and land-tenure pressure.

Cod Wars.outcome: Icelandic victory; UK accepted 200-mile Icelandic EEZ in 1976.
Cod Wars.aftermath: Three rounds of confrontation (1958-1961, 1972-1973, 1975-1976) between Iceland and the UK over fishing rights. Icelandic gunboats cut the trawls of British fishing vessels; the Royal Navy escorted trawlers. NATO mediation eventually forced UK acceptance of Iceland's extended fishing zone.

Cambodian–Vietnamese War.outcome: Vietnamese victory; Khmer Rouge driven from Phnom Penh January 1979.
Cambodian–Vietnamese War.aftermath: Vietnamese invasion ended Khmer Rouge rule and installed the People's Republic of Kampuchea. Provoked the brief Sino-Vietnamese War of 1979. Vietnamese occupation lasted until 1989.
Cambodian–Vietnamese War.keyTerms: Fall of Phnom Penh to Vietnamese forces (January 7, 1979)

Iran hostage crisis.outcome: Algiers Accords (January 20, 1981); hostages released after 444 days.
Iran hostage crisis.aftermath: See Iran hostage crisis as a diplomatic crisis rather than a war. The crisis defined US-Iran relations for decades and contributed to Carter's electoral defeat. The hostages were released minutes after Reagan's inauguration.

Operation Eagle Claw.outcome: US failure; mission aborted at Desert One, eight US servicemen killed.
Operation Eagle Claw.aftermath: The failed April 1980 US military attempt to rescue the embassy hostages in Tehran. The disaster contributed to Carter's 1980 election loss and produced the Special Operations Command reforms of the 1980s.

Falkland Islands sovereignty dispute.outcome: British sovereignty reaffirmed by the 1982 Falklands War.
Falkland Islands sovereignty dispute.aftermath: Two centuries of Anglo-Argentine sovereignty dispute over the Falkland Islands/Islas Malvinas. The 1982 war definitively confirmed British control; Argentine claims persist diplomatically into the 2020s.

Invasion of Grenada.outcome: US victory; new government installed December 1983.
Invasion of Grenada.aftermath: Operation Urgent Fury — a three-day US invasion of Grenada following the coup against the leftist People's Revolutionary Government. 7,600 US troops with eastern Caribbean allies removed the Hudson Austin regime; democratic government was restored within months.

United States invasion of Panama.outcome: US victory; Noriega captured December 1989; new government installed.
United States invasion of Panama.aftermath: Operation Just Cause — a five-day US invasion to remove Manuel Noriega. The operation involved 27,000 US troops and produced the first combat use of the F-117 stealth fighter. Noriega was extradited to Florida and convicted of drug trafficking.

Libyan Crisis (2011–present).outcome: Ongoing; rival administrations in Tripoli (GNU) and Tobruk/Benghazi (LNA).
Libyan Crisis (2011–present).aftermath: A decade-and-a-half crisis covering the original 2011 civil war, the post-Gaddafi militia order, the 2014-2020 second civil war, the 2020 Berlin Conference ceasefire, and the contested transitional process since.

Syrian civil war.outcome: Ongoing as of late 2025; Assad regime fell in December 2024 to HTS-led opposition.
Syrian civil war.aftermath: Fourteen years of war that began with anti-Assad protests in 2011 and ended with the lightning HTS offensive of late 2024. 600,000+ dead, half the population displaced, ISIS rise and fall, Russian/Iranian intervention, and the transformation of regional politics.
notable: Russian intervention reverses the war (September 2015)
Battle of Aleppo and the loss of the eastern districts (2016)
Chemical weapons attacks on Khan Shaykhun (2017) and Douma (2018)
Turkish operations against the SDF in northern Syria (Olive Branch 2018, Peace Spring 2019)
Lightning opposition offensive captures Aleppo, Hama, Homs, Damascus (Nov-Dec 2024)

Iraqi insurgency.outcome: Coalition / Iraqi government victory by 2011 withdrawal; insurgency mutates into ISIS by 2014.
Iraqi insurgency.aftermath: See Iraq War — canonical entry. The 2006-2008 surge under Petraeus was the period's tactical turning point; the political failure to integrate Sunnis after withdrawal seeded ISIS's rise.

Insurgency in the Caucasus.outcome: Russian victory; insurgency effectively suppressed by 2017.
Insurgency in the Caucasus.aftermath: A decade-long Salafi-jihadist insurgency in Russia's North Caucasus republics. Caucasus Emirate leader Doku Umarov was killed in 2013, the movement's remnants pledged allegiance to ISIS in 2015. By 2017 Russian operations and ISIS's collapse in Syria had ended large-scale attacks.

Ukrainian Kursk Oblast Incursion.outcome: Ongoing; Ukrainian forces hold a salient in Kursk Oblast through 2024-2025.
Ukrainian Kursk Oblast Incursion.aftermath: Ukraine's August 2024 cross-border offensive into Kursk Oblast — the first foreign army incursion into Russian sovereign territory since WWII. The operation diverted Russian forces from eastern Ukraine and put pressure on the Putin government domestically.

Sudanese Civil War (2023–present).aftermath: A war between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces that erupted in Khartoum in April 2023, after the breakdown of the joint transitional government. 150,000+ dead, 11 million displaced, full state collapse across Darfur.

Eight-Nation Alliance.outcome: Allied victory; Boxer Protocol signed September 1901.

Anglo-Spanish War (1761–1763).outcome: British victory; British seizures of Havana and Manila returned at the Treaty of Paris (1763).
Anglo-Spanish War (1761–1763).aftermath: A two-year extension of the Seven Years' War when Spain's Bourbon king honoured the Family Compact and joined France. Britain captured Havana and Manila but returned both at the peace in exchange for Florida.

Russo-Turkish War (1735–1739).outcome: Indecisive; Treaty of Belgrade (1739) returns most Russian gains to the Ottomans.
Russo-Turkish War (1735–1739).aftermath: Four years of war in which Russia retook Azov but was forced to renounce other gains by the simultaneous Austrian collapse and Ottoman recovery. The treaty held Russian expansion at bay for thirty years.

Russo-Turkish War (1828–1829).outcome: Russian victory; Treaty of Adrianople (1829) confirms Greek autonomy and Russian gains.
Russo-Turkish War (1828–1829).aftermath: A year of war that helped finalise Greek independence and gave Russia the eastern Black Sea coast and the mouth of the Danube. The treaty also confirmed the Sultan's recognition of Serbian and Romanian autonomy.

French invasion of Russia.outcome: Russian victory; the Grande Armée destroyed by winter and Kutuzov's scorched-earth retreat strategy.
French invasion of Russia.aftermath: Napoleon entered Russia with 685,000 men in June 1812 and crossed back over the Neman with under 40,000 in December. The catastrophe ended French dominance of Europe and produced the War of the Sixth Coalition that would finish him.

Hundred Days.outcome: Coalition victory at Waterloo; Napoleon abdicates a second time, exiled to St. Helena.
Hundred Days.aftermath: Napoleon's March 1815 return from Elba, ten weeks of campaigning, and final defeat. Marked the end of the Napoleonic era; produced the harder Second Treaty of Paris and Wellington's political career.

Bishops' Wars.outcome: Scottish victory; Treaty of Ripon (1640) leaves the Covenanters in occupation of Northumberland and Durham.
Bishops' Wars.aftermath: Two short wars over Charles I's attempt to impose an Anglican prayer book on Presbyterian Scotland. The Crown's fiscal crisis from the wars forced the recall of Parliament after eleven years of personal rule — the precondition for the English Civil War.

English Civil War.outcome: Parliamentarian victory across all three civil wars; execution of Charles I (January 30, 1649).
English Civil War.aftermath: A decade of war and rule under the Commonwealth and Protectorate. The wars produced the modern English constitutional settlement after the 1660 Restoration and 1688 Glorious Revolution — sovereign Parliament, no standing army without consent, no Catholic monarch.

Third English Civil War.outcome: Parliamentarian victory at Worcester (September 1651); Charles II flees to France.
Third English Civil War.aftermath: The Scottish-Royalist coalition's last stand. Worcester ended Stuart resistance until the Restoration nine years later; Cromwell's subsequent regime ruled as the Commonwealth and Protectorate.

Glorious Revolution.outcome: William of Orange takes the English throne; James II flees to France.
Glorious Revolution.aftermath: A fifteen-week political-military transformation in which William of Orange landed at Torbay with a Dutch army and James II's regime collapsed. The 1689 Bill of Rights, the Toleration Act, and the constitutional settlement that ended divine-right monarchy in England — landmark moments of liberal constitutional history.

Williamite War in Ireland.outcome: Williamite victory; Treaty of Limerick (1691) ends Jacobite resistance.
Williamite War in Ireland.aftermath: Two years of war between Williamite Protestant and Jacobite Catholic forces in Ireland. The Battle of the Boyne (July 1690) is the foundational event of Ulster Unionist identity; the post-war Penal Laws subjugated Catholic Ireland for the next century.

Chilean War of Independence.outcome: Chilean victory; San Martín–O'Higgins forces defeat royalists at Maipú (April 1818).
Chilean War of Independence.aftermath: A decade of war that ended Spanish rule in Chile. O'Higgins became Supreme Director and laid the constitutional foundation of the Chilean state.

Bolivian War of Independence.outcome: Bolivian victory; Bolívar's lieutenant Sucre declares independence August 6, 1825.
Bolivian War of Independence.aftermath: Sixteen years of guerrilla and conventional war ended with Sucre's victory at Tumusla. The new republic was named after Simón Bolívar and adopted his liberal constitution.

War of the Pacific.outcome: Chilean victory; Treaty of Ancón (1883) cedes Bolivia's coastal province and Peru's Tarapacá to Chile.
War of the Pacific.aftermath: Five years of war over Atacama nitrate deposits. Chile emerged the dominant South American power; Bolivia lost its coastline (still a grievance in Bolivian politics); Peru lost Tarapacá. The nitrate-fueled Chilean fiscal boom of the 1880s-1910s built modern Chile.

Ecuadorian–Peruvian War.outcome: Peruvian victory; Rio Protocol (1942) sets the modern border.
Ecuadorian–Peruvian War.aftermath: A six-week war in 1941 over the Amazon-basin border. The Rio Protocol awarded most disputed territory to Peru. The border remained contested through the Paquisha War (1981) and Cenepa War (1995) until the 1998 Brasilia agreement.

Yuan dynasty.outcome: Mongol-Yuan rule of China ended 1368 by the Ming.
Yuan dynasty.aftermath: Kublai Khan's dynasty ruled all of China for less than a century but reshaped the world: Mongol administration produced the Yam relay system, Pax Mongolica trade, Marco Polo's Travels, the integration of Yunnan and Tibet, and the institutions the Ming would inherit. Population decline under Yuan rule contributed to its collapse during the Red Turban Rebellion.

Red Turban Rebellion.outcome: Ming victory under Zhu Yuanzhang, who proclaimed himself Hongwu Emperor in 1368.
Red Turban Rebellion.aftermath: The rebellion broke Mongol Yuan rule over China and produced the Ming dynasty. Death toll estimates of 30 million reflect a generation of millenarian peasant war compounded by famine and plague.

Manchu conquest of China.outcome: Manchu victory; Qing dynasty established as ruler of all China.
Manchu conquest of China.aftermath: Same arc as the Ming-Qing transition. The conquest absorbed the Ming bureaucracy wholesale but layered a Manchu military aristocracy on top, with the eight-banner system the institutional backbone of Qing power for a century and a half.

Maratha Empire.outcome: Defeated by the British East India Company in three Anglo-Maratha wars (1775-1818).
Maratha Empire.aftermath: Founded by Shivaji in the 17th century, the Maratha Confederacy rose to dominate India in the 18th, then fragmented under British and internal pressure. The British conquest of the Marathas effectively ended indigenous Indian great-power resistance until 1947. Cumulative deaths across Maratha wars exceed 1.5 million.

Sino-Tibetan War.outcome: Inconclusive; Truce of Sungpan (1932) freezes the eastern Tibetan border.
Sino-Tibetan War.aftermath: A two-year war between the warlord governors of Sichuan and Qinghai and the Tibetan government over Kham and Amdo. The truce held until the People's Liberation Army invaded Tibet in 1950.

Scramble for Africa.outcome: Almost the entire continent divided among Britain, France, Belgium, Germany, Portugal, Italy, and Spain by 1914. Ethiopia and Liberia alone retained independence.
Scramble for Africa.aftermath: Three decades of European imperial conquest, justified at the Berlin Conference (1884-1885), produced arbitrary borders that still organise modern African politics. Estimated 10 million dead across King Leopold's Congo Free State alone; tens of millions more from disruption, famine, and resistance wars from the Mahdists to the Herero.

Second Italo-Ethiopian War.outcome: Italian victory; Ethiopia annexed into Italian East Africa, May 1936.
Second Italo-Ethiopian War.aftermath: Mussolini's war of revenge for Adwa. Italian use of mustard gas against Ethiopian forces and civilians. The League of Nations' failure to enforce sanctions discredited collective security and emboldened the Axis powers. Italian rule lasted only until British East African forces liberated the country in 1941.
Second Italo-Ethiopian War.keyTerms: Fall of Addis Ababa (May 5, 1936); Italian liberation (1941)

Mau Mau Uprising.outcome: British military victory; political settlement led to Kenyan independence (1963).
Mau Mau Uprising.aftermath: Eight years of Kikuyu-led revolt against British colonial rule and white settler land seizures. British counter-insurgency killed at least 25,000 (likely many more) and detained tens of thousands in "screening" camps. The war's political success forced London to grant independence to Jomo Kenyatta's government in 1963.

Biafran War.outcome: Federal Nigerian victory; Biafra surrendered January 1970.
Biafran War.aftermath: A thirty-month secession war that produced the first televised famine in the West. Three million dead, the vast majority Igbo civilians lost to starvation under a federal blockade. The war shaped postwar Nigerian politics and the international humanitarian-NGO sector that grew up around it.

Rwandan Civil War.outcome: RPF victory; Hutu Power government overthrown July 1994.
Rwandan Civil War.aftermath: Four years of war that began with the 1990 RPF invasion from Uganda and ended with the RPF takeover of Kigali after the 1994 genocide. Paul Kagame's government has ruled Rwanda since.
Rwandan Civil War.keyTerms: Arusha Accords (August 1993); RPF capture of Kigali (July 1994)

Rwandan genocide.outcome: RPF victory; Hutu Power government overthrown July 1994.
Rwandan genocide.aftermath: A hundred days of mass killing organised by the Hutu Power government killed 800,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus. The RPF takeover ended the genocide; two million Hutus fled to the eastern Congo, sparking the First and Second Congo Wars.

First Congo War.outcome: AFDL victory; Mobutu Sese Seko overthrown May 1997.
First Congo War.aftermath: Eight months of war that ended thirty-two years of Mobutu's rule in Zaire and renamed the country the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Laurent-Désiré Kabila took power; within a year his break with his Rwandan and Ugandan sponsors triggered the Second Congo War.

Second Congo War.outcome: Stalemate ended by the Pretoria Accord (2002) and the Sun City Agreement (2003).
Second Congo War.aftermath: Sometimes called Africa's World War. Nine national armies and twenty-five militias fought in the Democratic Republic of the Congo over five years. Casualty estimates of 5.4 million reflect mostly indirect deaths — famine, disease, displacement — rather than combat. The eastern Congo has remained unstable since.

Burma campaign.outcome: Allied victory; Japanese forces in Burma surrender September 1945.
Burma campaign.aftermath: Three and a half years of jungle war from the Japanese conquest of Burma in 1942 to the Allied liberation in 1945. Slim's 14th Army produced the longest fighting retreat in British military history followed by the largest land battle in the Pacific theatre at Imphal-Kohima.

Libyan Civil War.outcome: Anti-Gaddafi victory under NATO air cover; Gaddafi killed October 20, 2011.
Libyan Civil War.aftermath: Seven months of war that ended Gaddafi's 42-year rule. UN Security Council Resolution 1973 authorised the no-fly zone. Post-war Libya descended into the Second Libyan Civil War by 2014.

Italian campaign of 1796–1797 in the War.outcome: French victory; Napoleon imposes the Treaty of Campo Formio on Austria.
Italian campaign of 1796–1797 in the War.aftermath: The campaign that made Napoleon. A junior general was given an underfunded army and won battle after battle — Lodi, Arcole, Rivoli — knocking Austria out of the First Coalition single-handed.

Flanders campaign in the War of the Firs.outcome: French victory by 1795; Coalition forces driven from the Low Countries.
Flanders campaign in the War of the Firs.aftermath: Three years of war in the Low Countries during which French armies overran Belgium and the Netherlands, establishing the Batavian Republic. The campaign's humiliation drove Britain out of continental land warfare for years.

Indian Wars.outcome: US victory; Native sovereignty erased across the contiguous US by the 1924 Indian Citizenship Act.
Indian Wars.aftermath: Three centuries of intermittent conflict from the Jamestown frontier of 1622 to Wounded Knee (1890) and beyond. The wars produced the reservation system, the disappearance of buffalo herds, the surrender of Geronimo, the Indian Removal Act, the Dawes Allotment. 70,000+ killed, mostly Native.
Indian Wars.keyTerms: Wounded Knee Massacre (December 29, 1890); Indian Citizenship Act (1924)

Scottish Civil War.outcome: Covenanter victory; Royalist defeat at Philiphaugh (1645).
Scottish Civil War.aftermath: Three years of war in Scotland within the larger Wars of the Three Kingdoms. The Covenanter triumph at Philiphaugh ended Montrose's Royalist campaign and confirmed the Covenanter dominance until the Cromwellian conquest of Scotland six years later.

Spanish–Ottoman wars.outcome: Ottoman naval expansion in the Mediterranean countered by Habsburg Spain.
Spanish–Ottoman wars.aftermath: A century of intermittent Mediterranean war between the Spanish Habsburgs and the Ottoman Porte. Lepanto (1571) broke Ottoman dominance of the eastern Mediterranean; Tunis changed hands repeatedly. The wars exhausted both empires by the late 16th century.

Haitian Revolution.outcome: Slave revolt victory; independent Haiti proclaimed January 1, 1804.
Haitian Revolution.aftermath: The only successful slave revolution in modern history. Defeated French, British, and Spanish armies in turn. Toussaint Louverture's death in a French prison; Dessalines' independence proclamation. 162,000 dead. Haiti was the first Black republic and the second independent state in the Americas.

Islamic conquest of Persia.outcome: Arab Muslim victory; Sasanian Empire extinguished by 651.
Islamic conquest of Persia.aftermath: Twenty years of war that ended four centuries of Sasanian rule and brought Islam to the Iranian plateau. Yazdegerd III killed in flight; Persian culture survived under the new Islamic dispensation and shaped the Abbasid Caliphate that followed.
Islamic conquest of Persia.keyTerms: Battle of Nahavand (642); death of Yazdegerd III (651)

Magyar invasions of Europe.outcome: Magyar defeat at Lechfeld (955); settlement under King Stephen creates the Kingdom of Hungary.
Magyar invasions of Europe.aftermath: A century of mounted raids from the Pannonian basin into Central Europe and Italy. Otto I's victory at Lechfeld ended large-scale raiding and forced Magyar settlement; St. Stephen's 1000-1038 reign converted the Magyars to Christianity and founded the Hungarian kingdom.

Muslim conquest of Syria.outcome: Arab Muslim victory; Byzantine forces driven from Syria by 638.
Muslim conquest of Syria.aftermath: Four years of war that ended six centuries of Roman/Byzantine rule in the Levant. The Battle of Yarmouk (636) was the decisive engagement. The conquest produced the Umayyad heartland.

Second Northern War / The Deluge.outcome: Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth survived; Swedish gains rolled back by 1660.
Second Northern War / The Deluge.aftermath: Five years of war (1655-1660) that wrecked the Commonwealth — depopulated by 30%, partitioned and reoccupied by Swedish, Russian, Brandenburger, and Transylvanian forces in turn. The Polish-Lithuanian gentry recovered nominal control but the wars opened the slow path to the partitions of the 1770s-1790s.

Civil wars of the Tetrarchy.outcome: Constantine I sole emperor by 324; Tetrarchic system dissolved.
Civil wars of the Tetrarchy.aftermath: Eighteen years of civil war following Diocletian's abdication. Constantine's victories at the Milvian Bridge (312) and Chrysopolis (324) reunified the Empire and produced the Edict of Milan, the Council of Nicaea, and the founding of Constantinople.

Cromwellian Conquest of Ireland.aftermath: Three and a half years of campaigning that killed 15-20% of the Irish population through combat, famine, and disease. The Act of Settlement (1652) confiscated Catholic-owned land for redistribution to Cromwell's soldiers and creditors, producing the Protestant Ascendancy that would define Irish politics for three centuries.

Deluge.outcome: Treaty of Oliva (May 1660); Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth survives.
Deluge.aftermath: See Second Northern War / The Deluge.

Greco-Turkish War (1919–22).outcome: Turkish victory; Greek expedition into Anatolia routed; Treaty of Lausanne fixes Anatolian borders.
Greco-Turkish War (1919–22).aftermath: See Turkish War of Independence — canonical entry.

Han–Xiongnu War.outcome: Han victory; Xiongnu confederation split into Southern (Han client) and Northern (driven west) factions by 89 AD.
Han–Xiongnu War.aftermath: Three centuries of intermittent war between the Han dynasty and the steppe Xiongnu. The Han generals Wei Qing and Huo Qubing broke Xiongnu power in the late 2nd century BC; the wars produced the Silk Road as a Han-controlled trade artery and the Chinese imperial frontier strategy of envelopment and tributary control.
Han–Xiongnu War.keyTerms: Battle of Mobei (119 BC); Han-Xiongnu peace under Huhanye (54 BC)

Indonesian National Revolution.outcome: Indonesian victory; Dutch recognise sovereignty December 1949.
Indonesian National Revolution.aftermath: Four years of war and diplomacy after Sukarno's August 1945 declaration of independence. The Dutch "police actions" of 1947 and 1948 reconquered most cities but lost the political war as international (especially US) pressure forced the December 1949 Round Table Conference and transfer of sovereignty.

Ming-Qing transition.outcome: Manchu (Qing) victory. Beijing taken 1644; last Southern Ming pretender executed 1662.
Ming-Qing transition.aftermath: Forty-five years of rebellion, civil war, and conquest produced the Qing dynasty that would rule China to 1912. Manchu rule imposed the queue hairstyle by decree, integrated Mongolia and Tibet, and laid the foundations of modern China's borders. Twenty-five million dead by reasonable estimates.
Ming-Qing transition.keyTerms: Fall of Beijing (1644); death of Yongli (1662)

Portuguese Restoration War.outcome: Portuguese victory; Habsburg Spain recognises Portuguese independence (Treaty of Lisbon, 1668).
Portuguese Restoration War.aftermath: Twenty-eight years of war restored Portuguese independence after sixty years of Habsburg union (1580-1640). Anglo-Portuguese alliance against Spain produced a lasting strategic partnership that survived into the 20th century.

Swedish–Norwegian War of 1814.outcome: Swedish victory; Convention of Moss creates the Sweden-Norway personal union (1814-1905).
Swedish–Norwegian War of 1814.aftermath: A two-week war by Sweden against Norway after the Treaty of Kiel transferred Norway from Denmark to Sweden. The Convention of Moss recognised the Norwegian constitution (May 17, 1814) within a Swedish-Norwegian personal union — the constitutional foundation of modern Norway.

Wars of the Three Kingdoms period.outcome: Jin reunification under Sima Yan in 280.
Wars of the Three Kingdoms period.aftermath: Same as Three Kingdoms — canonical entry.

Ecuadorian War of Independence.outcome: Patriot victory at Pichincha (May 1822); Ecuador joins Gran Colombia.
Ecuadorian War of Independence.aftermath: Twelve years of intermittent war ended by Sucre's victory at Pichincha. Ecuador entered Gran Colombia until that federation's collapse in 1830, then became an independent republic.

Indian campaigns of Muhammad of Ghor.outcome: Ghurid victory; Delhi Sultanate established 1206 after Muhammad's death.
Indian campaigns of Muhammad of Ghor.aftermath: Three decades of campaign that ended Hindu Shahi rule in north India and laid the foundation of the Delhi Sultanate under his slave-general Qutb al-Din Aibak. The Second Battle of Tarain (1192) was the decisive engagement.

Japanese invasion of Taiwan (1895).outcome: Japanese victory; Taiwan colonial administration established by November 1895.
Japanese invasion of Taiwan (1895).aftermath: Five months of resistance war by the short-lived Republic of Formosa against Japanese takeover after Shimonoseki. Japanese rule lasted fifty years until 1945.

Jihadist insurgency in Niger.outcome: Ongoing; July 2023 coup ended French security partnership.
Jihadist insurgency in Niger.aftermath: A decade-long jihadist insurgency along Niger's Mali and Burkina Faso borders. The July 2023 coup against President Bazoum produced a junta that expelled French and US forces and joined Mali and Burkina Faso in the Alliance of Sahel States.

Murid War.aftermath: See Caucasian War — canonical entry covering the broader 1817-1864 arc.

Palatinate phase of the Thirty Years' Wa.outcome: Habsburg victory; Frederick V of the Palatinate, the Winter King, exiled.
Palatinate phase of the Thirty Years' Wa.aftermath: The 1620-1623 phase of the Thirty Years' War in which Bohemia and the Palatinate were subdued. Maximilian of Bavaria received Frederick's electoral dignity and the Upper Palatinate, and the Catholic League stood at its post-medieval peak. The war's next phases would internationalise the conflict.

Polish-Ottoman War (1672–1676).outcome: Ottoman gains; Treaty of Żurawno (1676) cedes Podolia and southern Right-bank Ukraine to the Porte.
Polish-Ottoman War (1672–1676).aftermath: The last major Ottoman expansion in Europe. The annexation of Kamianets-Podilskyi shocked Catholic Europe and helped produce the Holy League that would end the Ottoman advance at Vienna in 1683.

Ridda wars.outcome: Caliphal victory; tribal Arabia reunified under Abu Bakr by 633.
Ridda wars.aftermath: A year of war by Caliph Abu Bakr to suppress tribal rebellions and false prophets across Arabia after Muhammad's death. The campaigns consolidated the early Caliphate and produced the army that would conquer Persia and the Levant.

Second Italo-Abyssinian War.aftermath: See Second Italo-Ethiopian War — canonical entry.

Sulla's Second Civil War.outcome: Sullan victory at the Colline Gate (82 BC); Sulla becomes dictator.
Sulla's Second Civil War.aftermath: Two years of civil war between Sulla and the heirs of Marius. Sulla's proscriptions killed hundreds of senators and knights; his reformed constitution lasted only until Caesar.
Sulla's Second Civil War.keyTerms: Battle of the Colline Gate (November 1, 82 BC)

Ulm campaign within the War of the Third.outcome: French victory; Mack's Austrian army surrenders at Ulm (October 1805).
Ulm campaign within the War of the Third.aftermath: A model French strategic envelopment — Napoleon marched the Grande Armée from the Channel coast to the Danube in five weeks and surrounded the Austrians before Russia could arrive. Two months later he won Austerlitz.

Unification of Norway.outcome: Harald Fairhair victorious at Hafrsfjord (c. 872); Norway unified under one crown.
Unification of Norway.aftermath: A decade of conquest by Harald Fairhair that produced a single Norwegian kingdom from a patchwork of petty kingdoms. The defeated chieftains and their followers fled in large numbers to Iceland, the Faroes, and the Hebrides.

United States occupation of Nicaragua.outcome: US withdrawal 1933; Somoza dynasty assumes power.
United States occupation of Nicaragua.aftermath: Twenty-one years of US military presence in Nicaragua, including the long war against Sandino's nationalist guerrillas. US withdrawal in 1933 left the Somoza-controlled National Guard in charge; the Somoza dynasty ruled until 1979.

War in Somalia.outcome: Ongoing as of late 2025; Federal Government of Somalia + AMISOM/ATMIS hold Mogadishu and major towns; Al-Shabaab controls much of the rural south and centre.
War in Somalia.aftermath: A successor war to the Somali Civil War that began in 2006 with the ICU's rise and Ethiopian intervention. The African Union mission has had 23,000+ troops on the ground; Al-Shabaab has carried out bombings as far as Nairobi and Kampala.

War of the Bar Confederation.outcome: Russian-Polish royalist victory; Confederation crushed by 1772.
War of the Bar Confederation.aftermath: Four years of Polish nobility revolt against Russian influence. Russian suppression was followed immediately by the First Partition of Poland (1772) — the first stage of the dismemberment that would end the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.

Anarchy.outcome: Treaty of Wallingford (1153); Stephen retains the throne, Henry of Anjou recognised as heir.
Anarchy.aftermath: Nineteen years of civil war between Stephen of Blois and Empress Matilda over the English crown. The treaty produced Henry II and the Angevin Empire — the largest territorial entity ever held by an English king.

Byzantine-Latin Wars.outcome: Byzantine victory; Constantinople retaken July 1261 by Michael VIII Palaiologos.
Byzantine-Latin Wars.aftermath: Six decades of war and parallel Byzantine successor states after the Fourth Crusade. The reconstituted Byzantine Empire was a regional power on the Aegean shore, never fully recovering the territory or wealth lost in 1204.

Cimbrian War.outcome: Roman victory under Marius at Aquae Sextiae (102 BC) and Vercellae (101 BC).
Cimbrian War.aftermath: A decade of Germanic invasion that came closer to destroying the Roman Republic than any threat before Hannibal. Marius's reform of the legions during the war produced the professional army that would dominate the Mediterranean for the next four centuries — and provide Caesar his political base.

Finnish War (Napoleonic Wars).outcome: Russian victory; Sweden cedes Finland in the Treaty of Fredrikshamn (1809).
Finnish War (Napoleonic Wars).aftermath: Fourteen months of war that ended six centuries of Swedish rule in Finland. Alexander I created the Grand Duchy of Finland with a remarkable degree of autonomy that lasted until 1899 — the foundation of modern Finnish national institutions.

Franco-Turkish War.outcome: Turkish victory; Treaty of Ankara (1921) cedes Cilicia from the French mandate.
Franco-Turkish War.aftermath: A two-year war (1919-1921) between France and the Turkish National Movement in Cilicia and along the Syrian frontier. France's withdrawal was part of the larger Allied retreat from Anatolia that produced the Treaty of Lausanne.

Golden Age of Piracy.outcome: Atlantic state suppression of piracy by the 1720s.
Golden Age of Piracy.aftermath: Eight decades of opportunistic piracy in the Caribbean, off the West African coast, and along the Indian Ocean route — Henry Morgan, Blackbeard, Bart Roberts, Mary Read. The Royal Navy's sustained anti-piracy campaign of the 1710s-1720s shut it down.

Great Trek.outcome: Boer migration successful; Boer republics established in the Transvaal and Orange Free State by 1854.
Great Trek.aftermath: Two decades of organised Boer migration north out of Cape Colony to escape British rule, accompanied by intermittent war with Zulu, Ndebele, and other African polities. The Sand River Convention (1852) and Bloemfontein Convention (1854) recognised the new Boer republics.

Mongol invasion of Poland.outcome: Mongol victory at Legnica (1241); Mongols withdraw east on the death of Great Khan Ögedei.
Mongol invasion of Poland.aftermath: A year of devastation across Poland and Hungary. The death of Ögedei in Karakorum recalled the Mongol commanders for the succession, sparing central Europe from sustained Mongol rule.

Norman conquest of southern Italy.outcome: Norman victory; Roger II crowned king of Sicily 1130.
Norman conquest of southern Italy.aftermath: A century and a half of conquest by Norman mercenaries that produced the Kingdom of Sicily, ruled from Palermo as a cosmopolitan Norman-Arab-Byzantine state. The Hauteville dynasty held it until the Hohenstaufen succession a century later.

Northern War of 1655–1660 / The Deluge.aftermath: See Second Northern War / The Deluge.

Piracy in Asia.outcome: Ongoing as low-intensity maritime crime; large-scale piracy suppressed by the 1860s.
Piracy in Asia.aftermath: Three centuries of intermittent piracy in the South China Sea, Strait of Malacca, and Sulu Sea. Qing and European naval campaigns of the mid-19th century broke the great pirate confederations. Modern piracy persists at a much lower scale.
Piracy in Asia.keyTerms: Suppression of Cheng I Sao's fleet (1810)

Pomeranian War (Seven Years' War).outcome: Inconclusive; status quo ante restored at Treaty of Hamburg (1762).
Pomeranian War (Seven Years' War).aftermath: Sweden's contribution to the Seven Years' War, attempting to recover Pomerania from Prussia. The war ended with no Swedish gains and was a strategic mistake that drained the Swedish treasury.

Roman-Gaulish wars.outcome: Roman victory; Gaul integrated into the Empire by 50 BC.
Roman-Gaulish wars.aftermath: Four centuries of contact and conflict — from the sack of Rome by Brennus in 390 BC to Caesar's eight-year subjugation of Gaul. Caesar reported a million Gallic dead in his Gallic Wars and another million enslaved. Romanised Gaul became the bedrock of imperial Latin culture and, ultimately, France.

Second Libyan Civil War.outcome: Inconclusive; 2020 ceasefire and ongoing transitional process.
Second Libyan Civil War.aftermath: Six years of war between the Tripoli-based GNA/GNU and the LNA under Haftar. Foreign intervention (Russia, Turkey, UAE, Egypt) shaped the conflict; the 2020 ceasefire and the Berlin Conference framework produced a fragile transitional government.

Spanish invasion of Portugal.outcome: Spanish victory; Treaty of Fontainebleau (October 1807) and Spanish withdrawal.
Spanish invasion of Portugal.aftermath: The "War of the Oranges" of 1801 — a brief and decisive Spanish invasion under Manuel Godoy. Portugal closed her ports to British shipping and ceded Olivenza to Spain.

Spring and Autumn period.outcome: Disintegration of Zhou central authority; transition to the Warring States period.
Spring and Autumn period.aftermath: Three centuries of declining Zhou rule and rising regional state competition. The era produced Confucius, Laozi, and Sun Tzu — the foundational political and military thought of East Asia. By 481 BC the Zhou king's authority was nominal; the seven Warring States would fight on until Qin unification in 221 BC.

Thirteen Years' War.outcome: Polish victory; Treaty of Thorn (1466) cedes Royal Prussia and Warmia from the Teutonic Order to Poland.
Thirteen Years' War.aftermath: Thirteen years of war between Poland and the Teutonic Order, ending with Polish gains along the Vistula and the Order reduced to a Polish vassal. The treaty paved the way for the secularisation of the Order under Albert of Brandenburg in 1525.

Unification of Nepal.outcome: Gorkha victory; modern Nepal's borders set by 1816.
Unification of Nepal.aftermath: Seventy-three years of conquest by Prithvi Narayan Shah and his Gorkha successors. The Anglo-Nepalese War (1814-1816) fixed Nepal's southern border with British India; Nepalese independence and the Gorkha military tradition survived into the 21st century.

United Irishmen Rebellion.outcome: British victory; rebellion crushed by autumn 1798.
United Irishmen Rebellion.aftermath: Three months of revolutionary war inspired by the French Revolution. The defeat produced the Act of Union (1801) — Irish parliament abolished, direct rule from Westminster — and the long century of Irish constitutional and revolutionary politics that followed.

Arab conquest of Egypt.outcome: Arab Muslim victory; Alexandria surrendered November 642.
Arab conquest of Egypt.aftermath: Two years of war that ended Byzantine rule in Egypt. Coptic Christianity survived but the demographic and political transformation was decisive: Egypt has been Arabic-speaking and majority-Muslim ever since.

Chalukya-Chola Wars.outcome: Chola dominance into the 12th century; Western Chalukya collapse leaves Cholas regional hegemon.
Chalukya-Chola Wars.aftermath: A century and a half of war between the Western Chalukya and Chola dynasties of southern India. The Chola maritime expansion to Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia in the 11th century was the high-water mark of South Indian state power before European arrival.
Chalukya-Chola Wars.keyTerms: Chola conquest of Lanka (1017); Battle of Koppam (1054)

Dano-Swedish War of 1808–09.outcome: Inconclusive; Treaty of Jönköping restores status quo.

Egyptian–Babylonian wars.outcome: Babylonian victory at Carchemish (605 BC); Egyptian withdrawal from the Levant.
Egyptian–Babylonian wars.aftermath: Forty years of war between Saite Egypt and Neo-Babylonia for control of the Levant. The Babylonian victory at Carchemish allowed Nebuchadnezzar II to advance to the gates of Egypt and forced Egypt back to its Nile Valley heartland.

Fenian Raids.outcome: Canadian victory; raids fizzled out by 1871; helped catalyse Canadian Confederation.
Fenian Raids.aftermath: Five years of intermittent raids by Irish-American Fenians from US territory into Canada. The raids accelerated the British North America Act (1867) and Canadian Confederation as a defensive consolidation.

First Italo-Ethiopian War.outcome: Ethiopian victory at Adwa (March 1896); Treaty of Addis Ababa recognises Ethiopian independence.
