First Italo-Ethiopian War.aftermath: Three years of war that ended Italian colonial ambitions in Ethiopia and produced one of the few decisive African victories over a European army of the era. Adwa became foundational to pan-African and Ethiopian national identity.

Clan Cameron-Clan Mackintosh feud.outcome: Inconclusive; clan feuds extinguished after Culloden (1746).
Clan Cameron-Clan Mackintosh feud.aftermath: Three centuries of clan rivalry in the Scottish Highlands over Lochaber land. The feuds ended only with the post-Culloden destruction of the clan system.

Dano-Swedish War of 1808–1809.outcome: Inconclusive; Treaty of Jönköping (1809) restores status quo.
Dano-Swedish War of 1808–1809.aftermath: A peripheral theatre of the Napoleonic Wars. Denmark joined France after the British seizure of the Danish fleet (1807); Sweden joined the British alliance. The war ended with no territorial change between the Scandinavian states.

Gothic War of 376–382.outcome: Roman accommodation; Goths settled as foederati within the Empire by Theodosius.
Gothic War of 376–382.aftermath: Six years of war that began when Valens' army was destroyed at Adrianople (378) by Gothic refugees. Valens' death and the Roman defeat made it impossible to expel the Goths; Theodosius' 382 settlement permanently changed Roman frontier policy.

Great Prussian Uprising.outcome: Teutonic Order victory after fifteen years; Old Prussian society reduced to bondage.
Great Prussian Uprising.aftermath: A fifteen-year revolt by the Baltic Prussians against the Teutonic Knights' conquest. The Order's ultimate victory broke Prussian society and accelerated the German colonisation of the eastern Baltic. The Old Prussian language died out by the 17th century.

Guandu campaign.parent: Wars at the end of the Han dynasty
Guandu campaign.outcome: Cao Cao victory; Yuan Shao's forces destroyed.
Guandu campaign.aftermath: A 200 AD campaign that broke the dominant warlord of north China and made Cao Cao's consolidation of the north possible — the precondition for the Red Cliffs campaign eight years later.

Indian Rebellion of 1857.outcome: British victory; the East India Company's rule transferred to the Crown.
Indian Rebellion of 1857.aftermath: A year of mutiny and uprising across north India ended the Mughal pretenders and the East India Company. The Government of India Act (1858) put India directly under the British Crown, the Raj that would rule until 1947. Estimates of a million Indian dead reflect the savagery of British reprisals as much as the rebellion itself.

Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.outcome: Ongoing; Pakistan Army operations have reduced but not eliminated the TTP insurgency.
Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.aftermath: Two decades of war in Pakistan's northwest tribal areas, tied to the Afghan War next door. Pakistan Army operations Zarb-e-Azb (2014) and Radd-ul-Fasaad (2017) reasserted state control over Swat and Waziristan; cross-border TTP attacks intensified again after the 2021 Taliban takeover of Kabul.

Irish Clan Wars.outcome: English victory; Gaelic Irish lordships extinguished by 1607.
Irish Clan Wars.aftermath: Four centuries of intermittent war among Gaelic Irish clans, ended by the Tudor conquest and the Flight of the Earls (1607). The Plantation of Ulster followed, redistributing confiscated lands to Scottish and English settlers.

Japanese invasions of Korea (1592–1598).outcome: Joseon-Ming victory; Japanese withdrawal after Toyotomi Hideyoshi's death.
Japanese invasions of Korea (1592–1598).aftermath: Six years of war that devastated Korea, exhausted Ming China, and ended the careers of Hideyoshi and the unifiers of Sengoku Japan. Admiral Yi Sun-sin's turtle ships and the Korean naval campaign halted Japanese supply across the Tsushima Strait and turned the war.
Japanese invasions of Korea (1592–1598).keyTerms: Death of Hideyoshi (September 1598); Battle of Noryang (December 1598)

Modoc War (Indian Wars).outcome: US victory; Captain Jack hanged October 1873, Modoc relocated to Indian Territory.
Modoc War (Indian Wars).aftermath: A six-month war in 1872-1873 by Modoc Indians under Captain Jack who fled the Klamath reservation and held out in the lava beds of northern California. The killing of General Canby during peace talks made the war national news.

Mughal conquests.outcome: Mughal empire at its height under Aurangzeb (d. 1707) covers nearly the entire Indian subcontinent.
Mughal conquests.aftermath: Two centuries of conquest produced the wealthiest empire of the early-modern world and the architectural canon (Taj Mahal, Red Fort) that defines popular memory of pre-British India. Aurangzeb's wars in the Deccan exhausted the treasury and opened the door to Maratha rise and, eventually, British East India Company supremacy.

Nagorno-Karabakh conflict.outcome: Azerbaijani victory; September 2023 Azerbaijani offensive forces Armenian capitulation.
Nagorno-Karabakh conflict.aftermath: Three and a half decades of intermittent war between Armenia and Azerbaijan over the Nagorno-Karabakh enclave. The 2020 Second Karabakh War reversed Armenian gains; the 2023 offensive ended Armenian Karabakh entirely with the displacement of 100,000+ ethnic Armenians.

Occupation of Nicaragua.outcome: US withdrawal 1933; Somoza dynasty assumes power.
Occupation of Nicaragua.aftermath: See United States occupation of Nicaragua.

Piracy off the coast of Somalia.outcome: International naval suppression by 2017; piracy effectively halted by Combined Task Force 151.
Piracy off the coast of Somalia.aftermath: A decade of large-scale Somali piracy ended by international naval patrols (CTF-151, EU NAVFOR Atalanta) and the deployment of private armed guards on commercial shipping. Piracy attempts dropped from 237 in 2011 to near zero by 2017.

Polish–Russian War 1830–1831.outcome: Russian victory; November Uprising defeated, Polish autonomy revoked.

Reapers' War.outcome: French gain in Roussillon; Catalan grievances temporarily settled within Spain.
Reapers' War.aftermath: A twenty-year Catalan revolt against Castilian taxation and military burden during the Thirty Years' War. France absorbed Roussillon and Cerdagne; Spain reasserted control over the rest of Catalonia after 1659.

Red Cliffs campaign.parent: Wars at the end of the Han dynasty
Red Cliffs campaign.outcome: Sun-Liu alliance victory; Cao Cao's southern expedition halted.
Red Cliffs campaign.aftermath: The decisive battle of late Han China that fixed the three-power division (Cao Cao north, Sun Quan east, Liu Bei southwest) which would crystallise into the Three Kingdoms. Cao Cao's naval defeat in late 208 was the moment China's unification under Han slipped definitively out of reach.

Roman-Germanic wars.outcome: Mixed; Rome holds the Rhine frontier until the 5th century, then collapses.
Roman-Germanic wars.aftermath: Seven centuries of war on the Rhine-Danube limes. The catastrophic Roman defeat at the Teutoburg Forest (9 AD) fixed the Rhine as Rome's northern boundary; the Marcomannic Wars under Marcus Aurelius; the third-century invasions; the 5th-century migrations that produced the successor kingdoms.
Roman-Germanic wars.keyTerms: Battle of the Teutoburg Forest (9 AD); Sack of Rome (410 AD)

Roman–Alamanni conflict.outcome: Mixed; Alamanni eventually settled in southwestern Germany by the 5th century, absorbed into the Frankish kingdom.
Roman–Alamanni conflict.aftermath: Three centuries of intermittent war on the Rhine frontier. The Alamanni's defeat by Clovis at Tolbiac (496) brought their territory into the Frankish realm.

Russo-Swedish War of 1788–1790.outcome: Inconclusive; Treaty of Värälä (1790) restores status quo ante bellum.
Russo-Swedish War of 1788–1790.aftermath: Two years of war launched by Gustav III to recover Swedish territory lost to Russia. Despite Sweden's naval victory at Svensksund (the largest naval battle in Baltic history), the war ended with no territorial change.

Saudi–Rashidi War.outcome: Saudi victory; Rashidi emirate of Ha'il extinguished 1921.
Saudi–Rashidi War.aftermath: Two decades of war between Ibn Saud's Saudi-Wahhabi forces and the Rashidi rulers of northern Arabia. The Saudi capture of Ha'il completed the unification of central Arabia under the House of Saud — the foundation of the modern Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

Second Carnatic War.outcome: British victory; Treaty of Pondicherry (1755) confirms British dominance in southern India.
Second Carnatic War.aftermath: Five years of Anglo-French colonial war in southern India during the broader European peace between the Austrian Succession and the Seven Years' War. The decisive British victory under Clive at Arcot (1751) made the East India Company the dominant European power in the Carnatic.

Second Northern War.outcome: Treaty of Oliva (May 1660); Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth survives.
Second Northern War.aftermath: See Second Northern War / The Deluge.

Serbian–Ottoman wars.outcome: Ottoman victory; Serbia absorbed into the Ottoman Empire by 1459.
Serbian–Ottoman wars.aftermath: Nine decades of war ended at Kosovo (1389) by Ottoman victory and at Smederevo (1459) by formal annexation. Serbia would remain Ottoman until the 19th century.

Suvorov's Italian campaign in the War of.outcome: Russian-Austrian victory; French expelled from Italy by autumn 1799.
Suvorov's Italian campaign in the War of.aftermath: Suvorov's campaign drove the French out of Lombardy and Piedmont and threatened France itself before political mismanagement and the recall to Russia neutralised his army. Bonaparte's 1800 return at Marengo restored French Italy.

Texas-Indian Wars.outcome: US-Texan victory; Comanche and Kiowa confined to Indian Territory by 1875.
Texas-Indian Wars.aftermath: See Comanche Wars. The Texas Rangers and the US Army campaigns of the 1840s-1870s broke Comanche and Kiowa power on the southern Plains.

Transition from Sui to Tang.outcome: Tang victory; Li Yuan founds the Tang dynasty in 618.
Transition from Sui to Tang.aftermath: A decade of rebellion against Sui rule produced the Tang, often regarded as China's most cosmopolitan dynasty. The Tang held for almost three centuries and shaped East Asian political institutions, poetry, and Buddhism. Death toll estimates around 1.5 million reflect the brutality of Sui collapse.

Turkish–Armenian War.outcome: Turkish victory; Treaty of Kars (1921) confirms Soviet-Turkish division of Armenian territory.
Turkish–Armenian War.aftermath: Three months of war (September-December 1920) erased the short-lived First Republic of Armenia and divided its territory between Kemalist Turkey and Soviet Russia. Followed the Armenian Genocide of 1915-1920; together the events produced the modern Armenian diaspora.

Afghan–Maratha conflicts.outcome: Afghan victory at the Third Battle of Panipat (January 1761).
Afghan–Maratha conflicts.aftermath: See Indian Campaign of Ahmad Shah Durrani. The Maratha defeat ended their imperial ambitions and opened the Indian power vacuum that the British East India Company filled within fifty years.

Ahom-Mughal conflicts.outcome: Ahom victory; Saraighat (1671) checks Mughal expansion into Assam.
Ahom-Mughal conflicts.aftermath: Almost seventy years of war during which the Ahom kingdom successfully defended its Brahmaputra valley territory against repeated Mughal invasions. Lachit Borphukan's victory at Saraighat is foundational to modern Assamese identity.

American War of Independence.outcome: American victory; Treaty of Paris (September 1783) recognises American independence.
American War of Independence.aftermath: See American Revolutionary War — canonical entry.

Anglo–Spanish War (1585).outcome: Inconclusive; Treaty of London (1604) ends formal hostilities.

Bangladesh Liberation War and Indo-Pakis.outcome: Bangladeshi-Indian victory; East Pakistan becomes independent Bangladesh December 16, 1971.
Bangladesh Liberation War and Indo-Pakis.aftermath: Same as Bangladesh Liberation War — canonical narrative.

Brabant Revolution.outcome: Imperial restoration; Habsburg authority briefly reasserted before French Revolutionary armies overran the Low Countries (1794).
Brabant Revolution.aftermath: A short-lived revolt by the Austrian Netherlands against Joseph II's reforms. The United States of Belgium declared independence (January 1790) but collapsed within a year as conservative and progressive factions split. French Revolutionary armies arrived four years later.

Breton War of Succession.outcome: Montfortist victory; John IV recognised as Duke of Brittany (1365).
Breton War of Succession.aftermath: Twenty-four years of dynastic war within the larger Hundred Years' War, the English backing Montfort and the French backing Blois. The Treaty of Guérande confirmed the Montforts on the ducal throne.

British invasions of the Río de la Plata.outcome: Spanish-criollo victory; both British invasions repelled (1806, 1807).
British invasions of the Río de la Plata.aftermath: Two British expeditions to seize Buenos Aires and Montevideo during the Napoleonic Wars. Their defeat by locally-raised militias was a foundational moment in Argentine and Uruguayan national identity — a generation later the criollos that defeated the British declared independence from Spain.

Campaigns of Babur.outcome: Mughal victory at Panipat (1526); Babur founds the Mughal dynasty.
Campaigns of Babur.aftermath: Three decades of fighting from Fergana to Delhi. Babur's victory at the First Battle of Panipat (April 1526) ended the Delhi Sultanate and founded the dynasty that would rule most of South Asia for two centuries.

Campaigns of Cyrus the Great.outcome: Persian victory; the Achaemenid Empire emerges as the largest state of the ancient world by 530 BC.
Campaigns of Cyrus the Great.aftermath: Three decades of campaigning that produced the Achaemenid Empire from the Aegean to the Indus. Cyrus' takeover of Lydia (547), Babylon (539), and the lands of the former Median Empire created the political superstructure that would define ancient Persia until Alexander.

Chu-Han contention.outcome: Han victory at Gaixia (202 BC); Liu Bang founds the Han dynasty.
Chu-Han contention.aftermath: Five years of war between Liu Bang of Han and Xiang Yu of Chu after the fall of Qin. The final battle at Gaixia ended with Xiang Yu's suicide at the Wu River. Liu Bang founded the four-century Han dynasty, which produced the cultural template for what it has meant to be Chinese.
Chu-Han contention.keyTerms: Battle of Gaixia (202 BC); founding of the Han

Comanche Wars.outcome: US-Texan victory; Comanche resistance ended at the Battle of Palo Duro Canyon (1874).
Comanche Wars.aftermath: A century and a half of Comanche dominance of the southern Plains, broken finally by the Red River War of 1874-1875. The Comanches were confined to Indian Territory; Quanah Parker emerged as their last great chief.

Croat–Bosniak War.outcome: Washington Agreement (March 1994) ended hostilities and created the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
Croat–Bosniak War.aftermath: Two-and-a-half years of war within the larger Bosnian War in which Croat and Bosniak forces fought each other over central Bosnia and Mostar. The Washington Agreement reunited them against the Bosnian Serbs and produced the Federation that survives within Dayton Bosnia.

Franco-Spanish War (1635–59).outcome: French victory; Treaty of the Pyrenees (1659) cedes Roussillon and Artois to France.
Franco-Spanish War (1635–59).aftermath: Twenty-four years of war that broke Spanish dominance of Europe. The defeat at Rocroi (1643) ended the legend of Spanish infantry invincibility; the peace produced the marriage of Louis XIV to Maria Theresa and the path to French hegemony.
Franco-Spanish War (1635–59).keyTerms: Battle of Rocroi (May 1643); Treaty of the Pyrenees (November 1659)

German–Polish War.outcome: German victory; Treaty of Bautzen (1018) preserves Polish gains in Lusatia.
German–Polish War.aftermath: Two decades of war between Henry II of Germany and Bolesław I of Poland for control of the western Slavic borderlands. The treaty acknowledged Polish gains while reaffirming German suzerainty — a model for the contested border that defined Central European politics for centuries.

Hispano–Moroccan War (1859–1860).outcome: Spanish victory; Treaty of Wad-Ras (1860) enlarges Ceuta.
Hispano–Moroccan War (1859–1860).aftermath: A six-month war in northern Morocco that produced a Spanish indemnity, the expansion of Ceuta, and an enclave at Ifni. The war was a high-water mark of Isabelline Spanish prestige — quickly squandered.

Huguenot rebellions.outcome: Royal victory; Edict of Alès (1629) preserves religious tolerance but strips Huguenot political and military autonomy.
Huguenot rebellions.aftermath: A decade of religious-political war by French Protestants against Bourbon rule. Richelieu's siege of La Rochelle (1627-1628) was the decisive engagement. The Edict of Alès kept the Edict of Nantes' religious clauses but removed the fortified Huguenot strongholds — a critical step toward Bourbon absolutism.
Huguenot rebellions.keyTerms: Siege of La Rochelle (1627-1628); Edict of Alès (1629)

Indian Campaign of Ahmad Shah Durrani.outcome: Afghan victory at Panipat (1761) over the Marathas; Afghan empire withdraws from India shortly after.
Indian Campaign of Ahmad Shah Durrani.aftermath: Eight invasions of north India between 1748 and 1767. The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) shattered the Maratha confederacy at its peak and removed the only credible Indian challenger to British East India Company rule.

Indo-Pakistani war of 1947–1948.outcome: Ceasefire 1949; Kashmir partitioned along the Line of Control.

Kongo Civil War.outcome: Stalemate; the Kingdom of Kongo fragmented into competing factions, never recovering central authority.
Kongo Civil War.aftermath: Forty-four years of dynastic war in the Kingdom of Kongo. The Battle of Mbwila (1665) killed the king and shattered the unitary state. The fragmentation accelerated Atlantic slave-trade exports and ultimately produced the conditions for Portuguese colonial expansion.

Korean Independence Movement.outcome: Korean liberation 1945 — produced by Allied victory in WWII, not by the Korean movement itself.
Korean Independence Movement.aftermath: Thirty-five years of resistance under Japanese colonial rule. The March 1st Movement (1919), the Provisional Government in exile, and the Korean Liberation Army in China kept Korean nationalism alive but liberation came with the Soviet and US occupation of 1945.

Long War (Ottoman wars).outcome: Inconclusive; Treaty of Zsitvatorok (1606) confirms substantial Habsburg gains, Ottomans accept equality of address.
Long War (Ottoman wars).aftermath: Thirteen years of intermittent war along the Danube. The first Habsburg-Ottoman war the Habsburgs did not unambiguously lose. The settlement's recognition of the Habsburg Emperor as the Sultan's equal in dignity marked the slow turning of the long Ottoman tide.

Mexican Apache Wars.outcome: Inconclusive; Apache power in northern Mexico broken only by the US capture of Geronimo (1886).
Mexican Apache Wars.aftermath: Three centuries of war between New Spain (and then Mexico) and the Apache peoples of the northern frontier. The conflict consumed enormous Mexican resources and helped weaken the country during the US-Mexican War.

Military campaigns of Muhammad.outcome: Muslim victory; Mecca submits 630, Arabia unified under Islam by 632.
Military campaigns of Muhammad.aftermath: Eleven years of campaigns by the Prophet Muhammad and the early Muslim community from the Hijra (622) to the conquest of Mecca (630). The political unification of Arabia under Islam laid the foundation for the Rashidun conquests of the following decades.

Mongol–Jin War.outcome: Mongol victory; the Jin dynasty extinguished at the Siege of Caizhou (1234).
Mongol–Jin War.aftermath: The Mongols destroyed one of the largest empires of the era and incorporated north China into their growing realm. Population collapse in north China was severe — Chinese census records suggest 80% reductions in some provinces, an outcome that shaped Mongol policy on settled-agricultural rule for the rest of the campaign.

Muscovite–Lithuanian Wars.outcome: Russian gains; final settlement after 1537 fixed the eastern Lithuanian frontier.
Muscovite–Lithuanian Wars.aftermath: A century and a half of intermittent war as Muscovy rose and Lithuania declined. The wars produced the Russian gains of Smolensk, Chernihiv, and the lands east of the upper Dnieper.

Muslim conquest of the Maghreb.outcome: Arab Muslim victory; North Africa absorbed into the Umayyad Caliphate by 711.
Muslim conquest of the Maghreb.aftermath: Sixty years of campaign across Africa from the Nile delta to the Atlantic. The Berber peoples were eventually converted to Islam, and the conquest produced the springboard for the Arab-Berber invasion of Iberia in 711.
Muslim conquest of the Maghreb.keyTerms: Battle of Carthage (698); conquest of Tangier (708)

Nader's Campaigns.outcome: Persian victory across Mesopotamia, Caucasus, and India; collapse of Nader's empire on his assassination (1747).
Nader's Campaigns.aftermath: Nader Shah Afshar rebuilt Persia after Safavid collapse and conquered from Iraq to Delhi, sacking the Mughal capital in 1739 and taking the Peacock Throne. His paranoid late reign and assassination by his own officers ended Persian unity for a century.

Navajo Wars.outcome: US victory; Long Walk of the Navajo (1864) and treaty (1868) establish Navajo reservation.
Navajo Wars.aftermath: Two and a half centuries of intermittent war ended by Kit Carson's scorched-earth campaign in Canyon de Chelly (1864). 8,000 Navajos were forced on the Long Walk to Bosque Redondo before being allowed to return to a reservation on their homelands.

Israel–Hamas war.outcome: Ongoing as of late 2025; January 2025 ceasefire framework partially holds.

Russian War of Independence.outcome: Russian victory; Mongol Yoke ended at Great Stand on the Ugra (1480).
Russian War of Independence.aftermath: Two centuries of Mongol overlordship ended with the bloodless standoff on the Ugra River. Ivan III's subsequent consolidation of Muscovy produced the foundations of the modern Russian state.

Sino-Japanese War.outcome: See First or Second Sino-Japanese War.
Sino-Japanese War.aftermath: Either the 1894-1895 first war (see First Sino-Japanese War) or the 1937-1945 second war (see Second Sino-Japanese War).

Iran-Israel war 2024.aftermath: Eight months of direct Iran-Israel exchanges including the April 2024 Iranian missile/drone barrage (Operation True Promise) and Israeli counterstrikes on Iranian air defences. The most significant direct state-on-state exchange in the Iran-Israel rivalry since 1979.

War in Donbas (2014–2022).outcome: Frozen conflict until February 2022; superseded by the Russian full-scale invasion.
War in Donbas (2014–2022).aftermath: Eight years of low-intensity war in eastern Ukraine between Ukrainian forces and Russian-backed separatists in the Donetsk and Luhansk People's Republics. 14,000+ killed, 1.5 million displaced. The conflict was effectively absorbed into the wider Russo-Ukrainian War when Russia launched its full-scale invasion February 24, 2022.
War in Donbas (2014–2022).keyTerms: Minsk II Agreement (February 12, 2015); Russian full-scale invasion (February 24, 2022)

Mughal–Sikh Wars.outcome: Sikh ascendancy by mid-18th century with the rise of the Sikh confederacies (misls).
Mughal–Sikh Wars.aftermath: A century and a half of intermittent war between the Mughal Empire and the Sikh community, beginning with Mughal persecution of the Gurus and culminating in Sikh military dominance over Punjab. Banda Singh Bahadur's 1709-1715 uprising shattered Mughal authority in Punjab; the post-1748 misls established Sikh military supremacy that became Ranjit Singh's empire.
Mughal–Sikh Wars.keyTerms: Execution of Banda Singh Bahadur (June 1716); Battle of Chappar Chiri (May 12, 1710)

Spanish American wars of independence.outcome: Patriot victory across Spanish America; Spain retains only Cuba and Puerto Rico by 1825.
Spanish American wars of independence.aftermath: Fifteen years of war (1810-1825) by which the Spanish American colonies broke from Madrid. Bolívar's northern campaign produced Gran Colombia; San Martín liberated Argentina, Chile, and Peru; Iturbide independent Mexico; the Central American Federation followed. Spanish defeat at Ayacucho (December 9, 1824) effectively ended the wars.
Spanish American wars of independence.keyTerms: Battle of Ayacucho (December 9, 1824); Battle of Carabobo (June 24, 1821); Battle of Maipú (April 5, 1818)

Insurgency in the Maghreb.outcome: Ongoing; jihadist insurgency fragmented and weakened by 2017.
Insurgency in the Maghreb.aftermath: Sahel/Maghreb jihadist insurgency centered on AQIM and its splinters. The 2013 French Operation Serval in Mali pushed the insurgency south; the 2017 JNIM merger consolidated remaining factions. State authority in much of the Sahel collapsed after 2020 coups.

Sudan war (2023–present).outcome: Ongoing; SAF-RSF civil war devastating Khartoum, Darfur, and Kordofan.
Sudan war (2023–present).aftermath: Ongoing civil war between the Sudanese Armed Forces (al-Burhan) and the Rapid Support Forces (Hemedti) that began April 15, 2023. 10+ million displaced — the largest displacement crisis in the world. Famine declared in Darfur in 2024. The war is destroying the institutions of the Sudanese state.
Sudan war (2023–present).keyTerms: RSF assault on Khartoum (April 15, 2023); fall of El Geneina (June 2023)

Polish–Bolshevik War.outcome: Polish victory at the Battle of Warsaw (Miracle on the Vistula); Treaty of Riga (1921).
Polish–Bolshevik War.aftermath: Eighteen months of war between the second Polish Republic and Soviet Russia. Piłsudski's August 1920 victory at Warsaw saved Poland — possibly Europe — from Soviet conquest. The Treaty of Riga fixed the Polish eastern border that held until September 1939.
Polish–Bolshevik War.keyTerms: Battle of Warsaw (August 13-25, 1920); Treaty of Riga (March 18, 1921)

Roman-Parthian Wars.outcome: Long stalemate; Parthian Empire fell to the Sasanian Persians in 224 AD.
Roman-Parthian Wars.aftermath: Three centuries of intermittent war between Rome and the Parthian Empire over Armenia and Mesopotamia. The Roman disaster at Carrhae (53 BC) was offset by later campaigns under Trajan, Lucius Verus, and Septimius Severus. Neither side could permanently dominate; the Euphrates remained the practical frontier.
Roman-Parthian Wars.keyTerms: Battle of Carrhae (May 53 BC); Trajan's Parthian campaign (113-117 AD)

South African Border War.outcome: Inconclusive militarily; international pressure and Cuban/Angolan exhaustion produced the Tripartite Accord (December 1988).
South African Border War.aftermath: Twenty-three years of war (1966-1989) along the Namibian-Angolan border between South African forces, SWAPO, and Cuban/Angolan forces. The war was the major Cold War proxy in southern Africa. The 1988 Tripartite Accord linked South African withdrawal from Namibia to Cuban withdrawal from Angola, leading to Namibian independence (March 1990).
South African Border War.keyTerms: Tripartite Accord (December 22, 1988); Battle of Cuito Cuanavale (1987-1988)

Russian conquest of Siberia.outcome: Russian victory; Siberia fully under Russian control by the early 17th century.
Russian conquest of Siberia.aftermath: A two-century campaign by Russian Cossacks and merchants to extend Tsarist rule across Siberia to the Pacific. Yermak's 1581 expedition broke the Khanate of Sibir; Russian outposts reached the Pacific (Okhotsk) by 1639. The Treaty of Nerchinsk (1689) fixed the Sino-Russian border in the Far East.
Russian conquest of Siberia.keyTerms: Yermak's capture of Qashliq (1582); Treaty of Nerchinsk (August 27, 1689)

Warring States period.outcome: Qin victory; unification of China under the First Emperor in 221 BC.
Warring States period.aftermath: Two and a half centuries of war among the seven major Chinese states (Qin, Chu, Han, Zhao, Wei, Yan, Qi) following the collapse of Zhou central authority. Qin Shi Huang's relentless conquests under Li Si and Meng Tian unified China in 221 BC, founding the imperial Chinese state that has endured in some form for 2,200 years.
Warring States period.keyTerms: Qin unification (221 BC); Battle of Changping (260 BC)

Unification of Italy.outcome: See Italian unification / Wars of Italian Unification.

Pyramid Lake War.outcome: Paiute Confederacy defeated; Pyramid Lake Reservation established 1860.
Pyramid Lake War.aftermath: A two-month Paiute war in 1860 in present-day Nevada that ended with the establishment of the Pyramid Lake Indian Reservation. The Paiute won the first Battle of Pyramid Lake but lost the second; the war ended with a US-imposed peace.

Suvorov's Italian campaign during the wa.outcome: See Suvorov's Italian campaign in the War of the Second Coalition.
Suvorov's Italian campaign during the wa.aftermath: See entry under the canonical name.

Toyotomi Hideyoshi's Kyūshū Campaign.aftermath: A short 1586-1587 campaign by Hideyoshi to bring Kyushu under his control. The Shimazu clan, having nearly unified Kyushu, was forced to submit. Followed Hideyoshi's 1585 unification of Shikoku and preceded his 1590 unification campaign in the east.

Polish–Muscovite War (1605–18).outcome: Polish strategic victory; Truce of Deulino (1618).
Polish–Muscovite War (1605–18).aftermath: The thirteen-year war during the Russian Time of Troubles. Polish-Lithuanian forces briefly occupied Moscow (1610-1612); the Polish prince Władysław was elected Russian tsar before being expelled. The Truce of Deulino gave Smolensk and the Severia to Poland-Lithuania.
Polish–Muscovite War (1605–18).keyTerms: Truce of Deulino (December 11, 1618); Polish capture of Moscow (October 8, 1610)

Russian conquest of Central Asia.outcome: Russian victory; Khiva, Bukhara, Kokand all reduced to vassal/protectorate status by 1876.
Russian conquest of Central Asia.aftermath: Three decades of conquest (1839-1895) extending Russian rule across Central Asia. Russian forces captured Tashkent (1865), Samarkand (1868), Khiva (1873), and Khoqand (1876). The conquest closed the steppe frontier and brought Russia to the gates of British India — fueling the Great Game.

Six Days' Campaign within the Campaign o.outcome: Napoleonic tactical victories; strategic situation unchanged.
Six Days' Campaign within the Campaign o.aftermath: A six-day stretch in February 1814 during which Napoleon won four consecutive battles (Champaubert, Montmirail, Château-Thierry, Vauchamps) against scattered Allied corps. Brilliant tactical successes that could not reverse the strategic collapse of the Empire.

First Matabele War.outcome: British South Africa Company victory; conquest of Matabeleland and incorporation into Rhodesia.
First Matabele War.aftermath: A six-month war by the British South Africa Company against Lobengula's Matabele Kingdom. Maxim guns destroyed the Matabele warriors at the Shangani and Bembesi. The conquest brought Matabeleland into the new colony of Rhodesia.
First Matabele War.keyTerms: Battle of Shangani (October 25, 1893); Battle of Bembesi (November 1, 1893)

Mongol invasions and conquests.outcome: Mongol Empire reaches its greatest extent under Möngke (d. 1259); fragments after his death.
Mongol invasions and conquests.aftermath: Six decades of conquest under Genghis Khan and his successors that produced the largest contiguous land empire in history. The Mongol invasions killed an estimated 40 million people. The empire split after Möngke's death (1259) into four khanates that ruled for two centuries.
Mongol invasions and conquests.keyTerms: Sack of Baghdad (February 1258); Battle of Ain Jalut (September 3, 1260)

Cold War.outcome: Soviet collapse 1991; United States as sole superpower.
Cold War.aftermath: Forty-five years of US-Soviet rivalry that shaped global politics — proxy wars in Korea, Vietnam, Afghanistan, Angola, Nicaragua, El Salvador; nuclear arms race; space race; decolonisation; the collapse of European communism 1989-1991 and the Soviet Union itself December 25, 1991.
Cold War.keyTerms: Fall of the Berlin Wall (November 9, 1989); Dissolution of the Soviet Union (December 26, 1991)

Cuban Missile Crisis.outcome: Soviet withdrawal of Cuban missiles in exchange for secret US withdrawal of Jupiter missiles from Turkey.
Cuban Missile Crisis.aftermath: Thirteen days in October 1962 — the closest the Cold War came to nuclear war. The Kennedy-Khrushchev resolution produced the Moscow-Washington hotline (1963) and the Partial Test Ban Treaty (1963).

Israeli–Palestinian conflict.outcome: Ongoing; the central unresolved territorial conflict in the modern Middle East.
Israeli–Palestinian conflict.aftermath: Over 75 years of intermittent war between Israel and Palestinian Arab populations, encompassing the 1948 Arab-Israeli war, multiple Israeli-Arab wars, the First and Second Intifadas, the Oslo process, and the ongoing Israel-Hamas war that began October 7, 2023.

1982 Lebanon War.outcome: Israeli operational victory; PLO expelled to Tunis; sectarian war continues until 1990.
1982 Lebanon War.aftermath: Israeli invasion to expel the PLO from Lebanon. Reached Beirut in eight days; PLO evacuation under multinational supervision. The September 1982 Sabra-Shatila massacre by Phalangist militia under Israeli watch became a defining international incident.

French Revolution.outcome: Revolutionary republic established 1792; descent into Terror, Directory, then Napoleonic consolidation.
French Revolution.aftermath: A decade of revolution (1789-1799) that destroyed the Bourbon monarchy, abolished feudal privileges, declared the Rights of Man, executed the king and queen, fought a war on all fronts, and ended in Napoleon's coup of 18 Brumaire. The Revolution reshaped Europe more than any event since the Reformation.
French Revolution.keyTerms: Storming of the Bastille (July 14, 1789); Execution of Louis XVI (January 21, 1793); 18 Brumaire (November 9, 1799)

Anglo-Spanish War (1779–1783).outcome: Treaty of Paris (1783); Britain returns Florida to Spain; Spain keeps Menorca.
Anglo-Spanish War (1779–1783).aftermath: Spain's contribution to the American Revolutionary War. The Great Siege of Gibraltar failed; Spain captured Pensacola, Baton Rouge, and Mobile. The peace returned Florida to Spanish rule for the next 40 years.
Anglo-Spanish War (1779–1783).keyTerms: Treaty of Paris (September 3, 1783); Great Siege of Gibraltar (1779-1783)

War on Terror.outcome: Ongoing; declared aim of eliminating al-Qaeda largely achieved by mid-2010s; broader regional instability persists.
War on Terror.aftermath: Two-decade global counter-terror campaign launched after September 11, 2001 — including the Afghanistan War, the Iraq War, drone campaigns in Pakistan/Yemen/Somalia, the rise and defeat of ISIS, and an enormous expansion of US/Western intelligence and special-operations capabilities.
War on Terror.keyTerms: September 11 attacks (2001); Death of Osama bin Laden (May 2, 2011); Fall of Kabul (August 15, 2021)

Hittite Wars.outcome: Bronze Age Collapse (c. 1200 BC) ends the Hittite Empire.
Hittite Wars.aftermath: A succession of conflicts between the Hittite Empire and its neighbors — Mitanni, Egypt, the Assyrians, the Sea Peoples — across the 14th and 13th centuries BC. The Battle of Kadesh (1274 BC) produced the world's oldest surviving peace treaty between two states.
Hittite Wars.keyTerms: Battle of Kadesh (1274 BC); Egyptian-Hittite Treaty (c. 1259 BC)

Later Israelite Campaigns.outcome: Saul and David consolidate the Israelite kingdom.
Later Israelite Campaigns.aftermath: A series of campaigns by Saul and David recorded in 1 Samuel — battles against the Philistines, Ammonites, and Amalekites that established the early Israelite kingdom.

Jeroboam's Revolt.outcome: Division of the United Monarchy into Israel (north) and Judah (south), c. 931 BC.
Jeroboam's Revolt.aftermath: The succession war following Solomon's death produced the two kingdoms of Israel and Judah, dynastically and religiously distinct, that lasted until the Assyrian conquest of Israel (722 BC) and the Babylonian conquest of Judah (586 BC).

Sennacherib's campaign in the Levant.outcome: Assyrian victory; Hezekiah pays tribute; Jerusalem spared.
Sennacherib's campaign in the Levant.aftermath: Sennacherib's 701 BC western campaign devastated 46 fortified cities of Judah; only Jerusalem held out. Biblical, Assyrian, and Greek accounts agree on the strategic outcome; the cause of the Assyrian withdrawal from Jerusalem remains debated.
Sennacherib's campaign in the Levant.keyTerms: Assyrian siege of Jerusalem (701 BC); Lachish reliefs

Second Messenian War.outcome: Spartan victory; Messenia reduced to helotage for the next three centuries.
Second Messenian War.aftermath: A generation-long Messenian revolt against Spartan rule. The Spartan victory cemented the helot system that defined Spartan society until the Theban liberation of Messene (369 BC).

Spanish Empire.outcome: Empire dissolved across the 19th and 20th centuries; final imperial losses Cuba/Philippines (1898), Spanish Sahara (1975).
Spanish Empire.aftermath: A four-century imperial structure that at its 1500s peak governed the largest contiguous empire of the early modern era. The Spanish Empire collapsed in stages — Latin American independence 1810-1825, 1898 Spanish-American War, decolonisation of Africa 1956-1975.
Spanish Empire.keyTerms: Treaty of Paris (December 10, 1898); Independence of Spanish Sahara (February 26, 1976)

Roman–Etruscan Wars.outcome: Roman victory; Etruria absorbed by 264 BC.
Roman–Etruscan Wars.aftermath: Three centuries of intermittent war between the rising Roman Republic and the Etruscan city-states. Roman victory at Vadimo Lake (310 BC) broke the Etruscan League; by the First Punic War Etruria was Roman.
Roman–Etruscan Wars.keyTerms: Fall of Veii (396 BC); Battle of Lake Vadimo (310 BC)

Roman–Latin wars.outcome: Roman victory at the Latin War (340-338 BC); Latin League dissolved.
Roman–Latin wars.aftermath: A series of wars between Rome and the Latin League across the 5th-4th centuries BC. The decisive 340-338 BC war dissolved the league and absorbed Latium into the Roman state.

Tatar raids on the Commonwealth.outcome: Slave raiding continues until Crimean Khanate falls to Russia (1783).
Tatar raids on the Commonwealth.aftermath: Three centuries of intermittent Crimean Tatar raids into the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. The raids carried tens of thousands of Slavs to Ottoman slave markets each generation. Polish defensive structures (Sich Cossacks, fortifications) limited but never eliminated them until Russian conquest of Crimea.

The Troubles.outcome: Good Friday Agreement (1998); political settlement, paramilitary decommissioning.
The Troubles.aftermath: Thirty years of low-intensity war in Northern Ireland between Provisional IRA, Loyalist paramilitaries, and the British Army. 3,500 killed. The 1998 Good Friday Agreement institutionalized power-sharing and ended the campaign.

Hittite expansion under the New Kingdom.outcome: Hittite expansion peaks under Suppiluliuma I and Muwatalli II; collapses in the Bronze Age Collapse.

North African campaign.outcome: Allied victory; Axis forces in Tunisia surrender May 13, 1943.
North African campaign.aftermath: Three years of desert war from Libya to the Tunisian coast — Rommel's Afrika Korps, the British 8th Army, Operation Torch. The campaign closed the Mediterranean as an Axis lake, secured Suez, and gave the Allies the launching pad for the invasion of Sicily.

Indo-Pakistani war of 1965.outcome: Stalemate; UN-brokered ceasefire and Tashkent Declaration (January 1966).
Indo-Pakistani war of 1965.aftermath: A seventeen-day war over Kashmir initiated by Pakistan's Operation Gibraltar infiltration. The largest tank battles fought anywhere since WWII (Asal Uttar, Chawinda) ended inconclusively. The Tashkent Declaration restored pre-war borders.

Libyan Civil War (2011).outcome: NATO-backed rebel victory; Gaddafi killed October 20, 2011.

Mughal-Maratha Wars.outcome: Marathas survive Aurangzeb's 27-year campaign; Mughal exhaustion seeds 18th-century imperial decline.
Mughal-Maratha Wars.aftermath: Aurangzeb spent the second half of his reign in the Deccan trying to crush Shivaji's heirs. The Marathas held out, the Mughal treasury bled, and by 1707 the empire was overextended. Maratha expansion in the 18th century would fill the vacuum.
Mughal-Maratha Wars.keyTerms: Death of Aurangzeb in the Deccan (1707)

Russo-Swedish War (1656–1661).outcome: Status quo ante bellum; Treaty of Valiesar (1658) and Treaty of Cardis (1661).
Russo-Swedish War (1656–1661).aftermath: Two years of war during the Second Northern War in which Russia attempted unsuccessfully to seize Swedish Livonia. The treaty held until Peter the Great's Great Northern War four decades later.

Third Italian War.outcome: Habsburg victory; Peace of Cateau-Cambrésis (1559) confirms Spanish dominance of Italy.
Third Italian War.aftermath: Sixty-five years of war that began with Charles VIII's invasion of Italy in 1494 and ended with Spain dominant from Naples to Milan. The wars produced the modern military profession — the Spanish tercio, the Italian fortification school — and bankrupted both Spain and France.

Yemeni Crisis and the Yemeni Civil War (.aftermath: See Yemeni Civil War — canonical entry.

Third Anglo-Maratha War.outcome: Inconclusive; Treaty of Salbai (1782) restores status quo ante bellum.
Third Anglo-Maratha War.aftermath: Seven years of war that confirmed Maratha sovereignty against East India Company encroachment but exhausted both sides. The treaty held until the Second Anglo-Maratha War a generation later.

Byzantine–Serbian wars.outcome: Byzantine victory in 628 after centuries of intermittent war; Arab conquests follow.
Byzantine–Serbian wars.aftermath: Same arc as Persian-Roman wars and Roman-Sasanian War.

French protectorate of Morocco.outcome: Spanish consolidation of the protectorate by 1927.
French protectorate of Morocco.aftermath: Fifteen years of Spanish colonial war in northern Morocco, including the Rif War and the catastrophic 1921 defeat at Annual. The combined Spanish-French offensive of 1925-1927 finally subdued the Rif Republic; Spanish Morocco lasted until 1956.

Anglo-Spanish Wars.outcome: Inconclusive; Treaty of Seville (1729) restores status quo.
Anglo-Spanish Wars.aftermath: A two-year war over British commercial rights in the Spanish empire and the Spanish siege of Gibraltar. The treaty restored the asiento — the British slave-trade contract granted at Utrecht — until the next Anglo-Spanish war (1739).

Waterloo campaign during the War of the.outcome: Coalition victory at Waterloo (June 18, 1815); Napoleon surrenders.
Waterloo campaign during the War of the.aftermath: Hundred Days and Waterloo. Napoleon exiled to St. Helena; the Bourbons restored; the Congress of Vienna settlement preserved. The final defeat ended a quarter-century of European war.
Waterloo campaign during the War of the.keyTerms: Battle of Waterloo (June 18, 1815); Second Treaty of Paris (November 1815)

Islamist insurgency in Burkina Faso.outcome: Ongoing; multiple military coups (2022) reflect state collapse under jihadist pressure.
Islamist insurgency in Burkina Faso.aftermath: A decade of jihadist insurgency (JNIM, ISGS) that has displaced two million people and produced two coups in 2022 alone. Burkina Faso joined Mali and Niger in expelling French forces and shifted to Russian (Wagner/Africa Corps) security partnership.

Myanmar civil war (2021–present) and the.aftermath: A war between the State Administration Council military junta and the National Unity Government plus pre-existing ethnic armed organisations following the February 2021 coup. 60,000 dead, three million displaced, and the partial collapse of the military's territorial control in Rakhine, Chin, Kachin, and northern Shan states.

Somali Civil War (2009–present).outcome: Ongoing; the original 1991 civil war evolved into the War in Somalia after 2006.
Somali Civil War (2009–present).aftermath: Three decades of state collapse since the fall of Siad Barre in 1991. The war has produced perhaps 500,000 dead, the world's longest-standing collapsed state, and the piracy crisis off the Horn of Africa.

Assyrian conquest of Elam.outcome: Neo-Assyrian conquest of the Aramean kingdoms by Tiglath-Pileser III; Damascus falls 732 BC.
Assyrian conquest of Elam.aftermath: A century of Assyrian campaigns that destroyed the Aramean city-states of Syria and the northern Levant. The conquests produced the first true imperial structure in Mesopotamia and the deportation policies that scattered Aramean populations across the empire.
Assyrian conquest of Elam.keyTerms: Fall of Damascus (732 BC); Battle of Qarqar (853 BC)

Barcid conquest of Hispania.outcome: Roman victory; Hispania fully pacified under Augustus by 19 BC.
Barcid conquest of Hispania.aftermath: Two centuries of conquest from the Second Punic War to the Cantabrian Wars (19 BC). Hispania became a wealthy core province providing emperors (Trajan, Hadrian, Theodosius), grain, gold, and the philosopher Seneca.
Barcid conquest of Hispania.keyTerms: Numantine War (143-133 BC); Cantabrian Wars (29-19 BC)

First Anglo-Maratha War.outcome: Inconclusive; Treaty of Salbai (1782) restores status quo ante bellum.
First Anglo-Maratha War.aftermath: Seven years of war that confirmed Maratha sovereignty against East India Company encroachment but exhausted both sides. The treaty held until the Second Anglo-Maratha War a generation later.

Byzantine–Sassanid wars.outcome: Series of Roman-Byzantine vs Sassanian Persian wars; final Byzantine victory under Heraclius (628), but both empires were exhausted, opening the door for the Muslim conquests.
Byzantine–Sassanid wars.aftermath: Four centuries of intermittent war between the Romans/Byzantines and Sassanian Persia. The decisive 602-628 war under Heraclius (battles of Issus, Nineveh) ended in Byzantine triumph but devastation; both empires were broken when the Arab armies arrived in the 630s.

Italian Wars.outcome: Habsburg victory; Treaty of Cateau-Cambrésis (1559) confirms Spanish dominance in Italy.
Italian Wars.aftermath: Six decades of war (1494-1559) among France, Spain, the Holy Roman Empire, the Italian city-states, and the Papacy. The treaty cemented Habsburg Spanish hegemony in Italy for the next 150 years.

Assyrian conquest of Aram.outcome: Neo-Assyrian conquest of the Aramean kingdoms by Tiglath-Pileser III; Damascus falls 732 BC.
Assyrian conquest of Aram.aftermath: A century of Assyrian campaigns that destroyed the Aramean city-states of Syria and the northern Levant. The conquests produced the first true imperial structure in Mesopotamia.
Assyrian conquest of Aram.keyTerms: Fall of Damascus (732 BC); Battle of Qarqar (853 BC)

Roman conquest of Hispania.outcome: Roman victory; Hispania fully pacified under Augustus by 19 BC.
Roman conquest of Hispania.aftermath: Two centuries of conquest from the Second Punic War to the Cantabrian Wars (19 BC). Hispania became a wealthy core province providing emperors (Trajan, Hadrian, Theodosius), grain, gold, and the philosopher Seneca.
Roman conquest of Hispania.keyTerms: Numantine War (143-133 BC); Cantabrian Wars (29-19 BC)

Anglo-Spanish War (1727).outcome: Inconclusive; Treaty of Seville (1729) restores status quo.
Anglo-Spanish War (1727).aftermath: A two-year war over British commercial rights in the Spanish empire and the Spanish siege of Gibraltar. The treaty restored the asiento — the British slave-trade contract granted at Utrecht.

Yemeni Civil War (2014–present).aftermath: A decade-long war between the Houthi movement and the internationally recognized government, with Saudi-led coalition intervention (2015) and Iranian Houthi support. Mass humanitarian crisis; 377,000+ killed by 2022.
Yemeni Civil War (2014–present).keyTerms: Houthi seizure of Sana'a (September 2014); Saudi-Houthi truce (April 2022)

Myanmar civil war (2021–present).outcome: Ongoing; junta losing ground to NUG/PDF and ethnic resistance organizations.
Myanmar civil war (2021–present).aftermath: Civil war triggered by the February 2021 military coup against the elected NLD government. National Unity Government (NUG) leads resistance with allied Peoples Defence Forces (PDF) and longstanding ethnic armed organizations. As of 2025 the junta has lost effective control of much of the country.
Myanmar civil war (2021–present).keyTerms: Coup (February 1, 2021); 1027 Operation by Three Brotherhood Alliance (October 2023)

Spanish protectorate in Morocco.outcome: Spanish consolidation of the protectorate by 1927; ended with Moroccan independence (1956).
Spanish protectorate in Morocco.aftermath: Spanish colonial rule in northern Morocco, including the Rif War. The 1925-27 Franco-Spanish offensive broke the Rif Republic. Spanish Morocco rejoined newly independent Morocco in 1956.
Spanish protectorate in Morocco.keyTerms: End of the Rif War (May 1926); Moroccan independence (April 7, 1956)

Russo-Swedish War (1656–1658).outcome: Status quo ante bellum; Treaty of Valiesar (1658) and Treaty of Cardis (1661).
Russo-Swedish War (1656–1658).aftermath: Two years of war during the Second Northern War in which Russia attempted unsuccessfully to seize Swedish Livonia. The treaty held until Peter the Great's Great Northern War four decades later.

Jihadist insurgency in Burkina Faso.outcome: Ongoing; multiple military coups (2022) reflect state collapse under jihadist pressure.
Jihadist insurgency in Burkina Faso.aftermath: A decade of jihadist insurgency (JNIM, ISGS) that has displaced two million people and produced two coups in 2022 alone. Burkina Faso joined Mali and Niger in expelling French forces and shifted to Russian (Wagner/Africa Corps) security partnership.

War of the Seventh Coalition.outcome: Coalition victory at Waterloo (June 18, 1815); Napoleon abdicates and is exiled to Saint Helena.
War of the Seventh Coalition.aftermath: Three-month campaign that ended the Hundred Days return of Napoleon. Wellington and Blücher's victory at Waterloo terminated the Napoleonic era.
War of the Seventh Coalition.keyTerms: Battle of Waterloo (June 18, 1815); Second Treaty of Paris (November 20, 1815)

Polish-Ottoman wars.outcome: Inconclusive; Polish-Ottoman frontier stabilized at the Dniester River by the late 17th century.
Polish-Ottoman wars.aftermath: Three centuries of intermittent war between the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth and the Ottoman Empire over the Ukrainian and Moldavian frontier. Polish victories at Khotyn (1621) and Vienna (1683) checked Ottoman northward expansion; the Treaty of Karlowitz (1699) cemented the frontier.
Polish-Ottoman wars.keyTerms: Battle of Khotyn (1621); Battle of Vienna (September 12, 1683); Treaty of Karlowitz (January 26, 1699)

Viking expansion.outcome: Ended c. 1066 with the Norman Conquest of England; Viking world absorbed into Christian European order.
Viking expansion.aftermath: Three centuries (793-1066) of Norse raiding, trading, and settlement across the North Sea, Atlantic, Mediterranean, and Eastern European riverways. Founded Dublin, Iceland, Greenland, briefly Vinland; settled the Danelaw, Normandy, Rus' principalities, and Sicily. Christianization and the consolidation of European kingdoms ended the expansion phase.
Viking expansion.keyTerms: Lindisfarne raid (June 793); Battle of Stamford Bridge (September 25, 1066)

Somali Civil War.outcome: Ongoing; transitional federal government since 2012, but al-Shabaab and clan factions still control significant territory.
Somali Civil War.aftermath: Three and a half decades of war that began with the 1991 collapse of the Siad Barre regime. Includes the 1993 US/UN Operation Restore Hope and Battle of Mogadishu; the rise and ongoing insurgency of al-Shabaab; ATMIS/AMISOM peace-keeping operations. State authority remains contested.
Somali Civil War.keyTerms: Battle of Mogadishu (October 3-4, 1993); Founding of Federal Government (2012)

Thousand Days' War.outcome: Conservative government victory; Treaty of Neerlandia (1902) and Treaty of Wisconsin (1902) end the conflict.
Thousand Days' War.aftermath: Three years of civil war between Colombia's Liberal and Conservative parties. The war devastated the country economically and contributed to the 1903 separation of Panama (which the US then supported to secure the canal route).
Thousand Days' War.keyTerms: Treaty of Wisconsin (November 21, 1902); Separation of Panama (November 3, 1903)

Ottoman-Portuguese conflicts.outcome: Stalemate; Portuguese hold Persian Gulf strongholds (Hormuz lost 1622), Ottomans dominate the Red Sea.
Ottoman-Portuguese conflicts.aftermath: A century and a half of intermittent maritime war between the Ottoman Empire and Portugal across the Red Sea, Persian Gulf, and Indian Ocean. The Ottomans failed to dislodge Portugal from the Indian spice trade; Portuguese hold over Hormuz collapsed with Anglo-Persian assistance.
Ottoman-Portuguese conflicts.keyTerms: Capture of Aden (1538); Fall of Hormuz (May 1622)

Ottoman-Mamluk Wars.outcome: Ottoman victory; Mamluk Sultanate destroyed and Egypt + Syria absorbed into the Ottoman Empire (1517).
Ottoman-Mamluk Wars.aftermath: Three years of decisive Ottoman victory under Selim I that ended the Mamluk Sultanate of Egypt — a state that had ruled Egypt since 1250. Cairo became an Ottoman provincial capital; the conquest gave the Ottomans control of the Hejaz and the holy cities of Mecca and Medina.
Ottoman-Mamluk Wars.keyTerms: Battle of Marj Dabiq (August 24, 1516); Battle of Ridaniya (January 22, 1517)

Social War.outcome: Roman victory; Italian allies (socii) granted Roman citizenship.
Social War.aftermath: A three-year war (91-87 BC) in which Rome's Italian allies revolted to demand citizenship. The Romans crushed the revolt militarily but then granted nearly all the rebel demands, extending citizenship across Italy. The war directly precipitated Sulla's march on Rome and the civil wars that followed.
Social War.keyTerms: Lex Julia (90 BC); Lex Plautia Papiria (89 BC)

Sinhalese-Portuguese War.outcome: Inconclusive; Dutch intervention in the 1640s drove the Portuguese from coastal Ceylon.
Sinhalese-Portuguese War.aftermath: A century and a half of war between the Sinhalese kingdoms of Ceylon and the Portuguese Estado da Índia. Portuguese coastal control was finally broken by Dutch intervention; the interior remained the Kingdom of Kandy until the 1815 British conquest.
Sinhalese-Portuguese War.keyTerms: Battle of Mulleriyawa (1562); Dutch capture of Colombo (May 1656)

Russo-Turkish Wars.outcome: Series of 12 wars from 1568 to 1918; net Russian victory and Ottoman territorial collapse.
Russo-Turkish Wars.aftermath: See the specific wars (1768-1774, 1787-1792, 1806-1812, 1828-1829, 1853-1856 Crimean War, 1877-1878). The wars produced the modern Black Sea geopolitics, the independence of the Balkan states, and the long collapse of the Ottoman Empire.
Russo-Turkish Wars.keyTerms: Treaty of San Stefano (March 3, 1878); Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca (July 21, 1774)

Persian-Uzbek wars.outcome: Inconclusive; Khorasan stabilized as Safavid Persian territory by 1605.
Persian-Uzbek wars.aftermath: A century of intermittent war between Safavid Persia and the Shaybanid Uzbeks over Khorasan and Transoxiana. Shah Abbas I's campaigns in the 1590s-1600s secured Khorasan for Persia.

Ottoman-Saudi War.outcome: Egyptian/Ottoman victory; First Saudi state destroyed (1818).
Ottoman-Saudi War.aftermath: Seven years (1811-1818) of war by Egyptian forces under Muhammad Ali's son Ibrahim Pasha (on behalf of the Ottoman Sultan) against the First Saudi state and its Wahhabi religious movement. Ended with the destruction of the Saudi capital Diriyah and execution of the Saudi imam Abdullah bin Saud.

Illyrian Wars.outcome: Roman victory; Illyrian coast brought under Roman protection 219 BC.
Illyrian Wars.aftermath: Two short wars (229-228 BC, 219 BC) in which Rome suppressed Illyrian piracy along the Adriatic. The conquests gave Rome its first foothold in the Balkans, setting up the Macedonian Wars.

Wars of Italian Unification.outcome: Italy unified between 1859 and 1870; Rome the final addition.
Wars of Italian Unification.aftermath: See Italian unification — three wars (1848-49, 1859, 1866) plus Garibaldi's 1860 expedition and the 1870 capture of Rome.

Vandalic War.outcome: Byzantine victory; Vandal Kingdom of North Africa destroyed (534).
Vandalic War.aftermath: Belisarius's 533-534 expedition for Justinian destroyed the Vandal kingdom in eighteen months. The reconquered African provinces (Africa, Numidia, Mauretania) returned to Roman/Byzantine control and remained so until the Arab conquest a century later.
Vandalic War.keyTerms: Battle of Ad Decimum (September 533); Capture of Carthage (September 533)

War of Devolution.aftermath: Eleven-month war by Louis XIV against the Spanish Netherlands, exploiting an obscure inheritance claim. Limited French gains. The next Franco-Dutch War followed five years later.

War of the Camisards.outcome: French royal victory; Protestant rebellion suppressed by 1710.
War of the Camisards.aftermath: A seven-year Huguenot revolt in the Cévennes mountains of southern France against Louis XIV's religious persecution after the revocation of the Edict of Nantes. Crushed by Marshal Villars's combination of military force and selective amnesty.

Tudor conquest of Ireland.outcome: English victory; Treaty of Mellifont (1603) and Flight of the Earls (1607).
Tudor conquest of Ireland.aftermath: A century of conquest from Henry VIII's assumption of the Irish kingship (1541) through the Nine Years' War (1594-1603). The conquest produced the Plantation of Ireland under James I — the demographic foundation of the next four centuries of Irish-British conflict.
Tudor conquest of Ireland.keyTerms: Treaty of Mellifont (March 30, 1603); Flight of the Earls (September 14, 1607)

Umayyad conquest of Sindh.outcome: Muslim victory; Muhammad bin Qasim captures Sindh (711-713).
Umayyad conquest of Sindh.aftermath: Two-year Arab campaign that brought the lower Indus valley into the Umayyad Caliphate — the first Muslim foothold on the Indian subcontinent. Sindh remained nominally Muslim-ruled into the modern era and shaped subsequent Indo-Islamic civilisation.

Uruguayan Civil War.outcome: Colorado (Blanco) victory in the Guerra Grande; period of relative stability followed.
Uruguayan Civil War.aftermath: The Guerra Grande (1839-1851) — twelve years of war between the Colorado and Blanco parties that drew in Argentina (Rosas), Brazil, and Britain. Ended with Blanco surrender and the long Argentine intervention that produced modern Uruguay.

Victorio's War.outcome: US-Mexican victory; Victorio killed at Tres Castillos (October 1880).
Victorio's War.aftermath: A two-year war by the Chihenne Apache chief Victorio against US and Mexican forces in the Southwest borderlands. Victorio's death at Tres Castillos broke organised Chihenne resistance.

Unification of Saudi Arabia.outcome: Saudi victory; Kingdom of Saudi Arabia proclaimed September 23, 1932.
Unification of Saudi Arabia.aftermath: Three decades of conquest by Ibn Saud, beginning with the 1902 capture of Riyadh and culminating in the 1932 unification of Hejaz, Nejd, and the eastern provinces into the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

Unification of Hawaii.outcome: Kamehameha victory; Kingdom of Hawaii proclaimed 1810.
Unification of Hawaii.aftermath: Two-decade conquest by Kamehameha of the island chiefdoms, completed peacefully in 1810 when Kauai accepted vassalage. The unified Kingdom of Hawaii lasted until the 1893 US-backed overthrow.

Wars of the Guelphs and Ghibellines.outcome: See Guelphs and Ghibellines — canonical entry.

War of the Castilian Succession.outcome: Isabella I victory; Treaty of Alcáçovas (1479) recognises her crown of Castile.
War of the Castilian Succession.aftermath: Four years of war between Isabella of Castile and her niece Joanna la Beltraneja (backed by Portugal). Isabella's victory consolidated the Castilian-Aragonese union and produced the Catholic Monarchs.

Yellowstone Expedition of 1873.outcome: US Army survey completed under heavy Sioux harassment.
Yellowstone Expedition of 1873.aftermath: Custer's 7th Cavalry-escorted survey for the Northern Pacific Railroad. Cited as a precipitating provocation for the Great Sioux War of 1876.

War against Sigismund.aftermath: See Hussite Wars — Sigismund's coronation crusades against the Hussite Bohemians.

Viking Invasions of Ireland.outcome: Inconclusive; Norse settled the coastal towns (Dublin, Wexford, Waterford, Cork, Limerick) but were defeated at Clontarf (1014).
Viking Invasions of Ireland.aftermath: Two centuries of Viking raiding and settlement in Ireland. The 1014 Battle of Clontarf is the conventional end-marker of large-scale Viking power in Ireland; the Norse coastal settlements survived as Hiberno-Norse trading towns.

Wallachian Uprising of the Greek War of.outcome: Ottoman victory; Tudor Vladimirescu killed (June 1821) and the uprising crushed.
Wallachian Uprising of the Greek War of.aftermath: A five-month Wallachian peasant uprising led by Tudor Vladimirescu, parallel to the Greek war but with different aims. Its suppression nonetheless contributed to the wider Ottoman destabilisation that produced Romanian autonomy at the Treaty of Adrianople (1829).

War in Iraq.outcome: See Iraq War / War in Iraq (2013–2017) — see specific entries.

War in Somalia (2009-present).outcome: Ongoing; al-Shabaab insurgency continues against the federal government.

War of the Polish Succession (1587-1588).outcome: Sigismund III Vasa victory at Pitschen (1588); confirmed as king of Poland.
War of the Polish Succession (1587-1588).aftermath: A brief contested election after Stephen Báthory's death. Maximilian III of Austria challenged Sigismund III Vasa's election; defeat at Pitschen (1588) ended his claim.

War of the Straits.aftermath: A four-year war between Venice and Genoa for control of the Adriatic-Aegean trade routes. The Treaty of Turin confirmed Venice's long-term naval ascendancy in the eastern Mediterranean.

Tunisian–Algerian War (1705).outcome: Hussein I (Husainid dynasty) victory; consolidation of independent Beylik of Tunis.
Tunisian–Algerian War (1705).aftermath: A brief 1705 succession war that produced the Husainid dynasty of Tunis, which ruled until the French protectorate of 1881.

United States Exploring Expedition.outcome: Naval exploration mission; minor clashes with Fijian and other Pacific islanders.
United States Exploring Expedition.aftermath: Charles Wilkes's 1838-42 US Navy exploration of the Pacific, Antarctic, and South America. Largely scientific; collected specimens that founded the Smithsonian collections.

War between King Haakon the Good and the.outcome: Haakon's sons-of-Eirik victory at Fitjar (961); Haakon mortally wounded.
War between King Haakon the Good and the.aftermath: Three decades of intermittent succession war in 10th-century Norway between Haakon and Eirik's sons. Haakon's death gave the throne to Harald Greycloak, briefly, before the long Hákon Jarl regency that defined late-10th-century Norway.

War in the Vendée (Virée de Galerne).outcome: Republican victory; Vendéean army destroyed at Savenay (December 1793).
War in the Vendée (Virée de Galerne).aftermath: The October-December 1793 march of the Vendéean Catholic and Royal Army across Brittany and Normandy, seeking British landings that never came. The march ended in annihilation at Savenay.

Italian invasion of Albania.outcome: Italian victory; Albania annexed into the Kingdom of Italy as Italian Albania, April 1939.
Italian invasion of Albania.aftermath: Mussolini's five-day campaign deposed King Zog I and absorbed Albania into the Italian crown. Albania served as the launch base for the Italian invasion of Greece a year later. King Zog fled to Greece and eventually London. Albania was liberated by communist partisans under Enver Hoxha in November 1944.
Italian invasion of Albania.keyTerms: Italian landing at Durrës (April 7, 1939); Annexation proclamation (April 12, 1939)

Sudeten Crisis.outcome: Munich Agreement (September 30, 1938) cedes the Sudetenland to Nazi Germany without Czechoslovak consent.
Sudeten Crisis.aftermath: Hitler's third diplomatic victory of 1938 after the Anschluss and the Czech border crisis. The Sudetenland was annexed in October 1938, the rump Czechoslovakia broken up in March 1939 when German forces entered Prague. Chamberlain's 'peace for our time' became the byword for failed appeasement.
Sudeten Crisis.keyTerms: Munich Agreement (September 30, 1938); German occupation of Czechoslovakia (March 15, 1939)

Anschluss.aftermath: German troops crossed into Austria unopposed on March 12, 1938; the union (Anschluss) was declared the next day. Austria became Ostmark, then Alpine and Danube Reichsgaue. The international response was mostly acquiescence, emboldening Hitler's subsequent demands.
